title: AdverseVision-CoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Distributional Shift for Robust Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive demonstrates strong visual CoT reasoning under nominal conditions, but autonomous vehicles must operate reliably in adverse weather (fog, rain, snow, night), where future frame generation and trajectory planning degrade significantly due to distributional shift in both perception inputs and world model predictions. Textual CoT cannot capture degraded visibility dynamics; visual CoT approaches inherit this fragility.

Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseVision-CoT, extending visual spatio-temporal CoT with weather-conditioned future frame synthesis. A lightweight weather encoder (trained on paired clear/adverse image sets) produces a degradation embedding injected into the world model via cross-attention, conditioning future frame generation on predicted weather severity. We additionally introduce uncertainty-aware visual CoT: the imagined future frame is augmented with per-region confidence heatmaps rendered as additional visual token channels, allowing the inverse-dynamics planner to explicitly discount uncertain spatial regions during trajectory planning. Training uses a curriculum that progressively increases weather severity, with physics-consistent lane and object priors maintained under visibility constraints.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes-rain/night splits, OOD generalization benchmarks (Waymo adverse conditions), and synthetic corruptions (ImageNet-C style). Metrics include trajectory L2, collision rate, and FID under adverse conditions versus FSDrive and text-CoT baselines. Ablate weather conditioning and uncertainty channels independently.

title: CausalSceneCoT: Counterfactual Visual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving Scenarios
description:
Problem: FSDrive generates plausible future frames as visual CoT but only predicts the most likely future, lacking explicit reasoning about safety-critical counterfactuals (e.g., 'what if the pedestrian suddenly jaywalks?'). This limits the model's ability to plan defensively in rare but dangerous scenarios.

Method: We extend visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual branching. Given a current observation, the model generates multiple divergent future frames representing distinct causal interventions on scene agents (e.g., nominal trajectory, sudden braking, lateral intrusion). Each counterfactual frame is produced by conditioning the world model on explicit perturbation tokens that encode agent behavior hypotheses. A risk-weighted attention mechanism then aggregates across counterfactual branches to produce a trajectory that minimizes worst-case collision probability rather than expected error.

Experiments: (1) Nuplan closed-loop simulation evaluating reactive scenarios vs. FSDrive and UniAD baselines; (2) NAVSIM with injected adversarial agent perturbations measuring collision avoidance under distribution shift; (3) Ablation isolating number of counterfactual branches (1, 3, 5) vs. planning safety metrics; (4) Human evaluation of counterfactual plausibility using a newly curated edge-case driving dataset from real dashcam footage. Success metrics include reactive collision rate, displacement error, and FID of counterfactual frames.

title: AdverCoT: Stress-Testing Visual Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in VLA Models via Adversarial Future Frame Perturbations
description: Problem: While visual spatio-temporal CoT improves autonomous driving planning, it remains unclear how robust these imagined future frames are to distribution shifts, sensor noise, or adversarial perturbations. A VLA that plans from corrupted or hallucinated visual CoT could produce catastrophically unsafe trajectories, yet no systematic evaluation framework exists for this failure mode. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverCoT, a robustness evaluation and training framework that targets the visual CoT bottleneck. We design three perturbation families: (1) semantic adversarial attacks that subtly alter predicted 3D bounding box positions/orientations in future frames, (2) structural corruptions that remove or misplace lane dividers, and (3) photorealistic texture adversaries generated via a diffusion-based inpainter. We then propose Certified CoT Training, which augments the curriculum pre-training pipeline with adversarially perturbed future frames as hard negatives, forcing the inverse-dynamics model to develop invariance to plausible visual CoT errors. A consistency regularizer penalizes trajectory divergence between clean and perturbed CoT inputs. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM under all three perturbation families, measuring L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and CoT-to-plan consistency. Ablations compare standard FSDrive, adversarially trained variants, and an oracle with ground-truth future frames, quantifying the safety margin gained by robust visual CoT.

title: AdverCoT: Stress-Testing Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Robustness via Adversarial Future Frame Perturbations
description: Problem: While FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning, it remains unclear how robust these visual reasoning chains are under distribution shifts, sensor noise, or adversarial corruptions. A corrupted or hallucinated intermediate visual CoT frame could silently propagate catastrophic planning errors — a critical safety concern for deployment. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverCoT, a framework that systematically attacks and hardens visual CoT representations in VLA-based driving models. We design three attack categories targeting the visual CoT: (1) semantic attacks that swap predicted object boxes/lane dividers with physically plausible but incorrect configurations, (2) perceptual attacks injecting structured noise into future frame tokens while preserving FID scores, and (3) causal attacks that create temporally inconsistent predicted futures. We then propose a CoT-aware adversarial training procedure that augments the curriculum pre-training with adversarially perturbed visual CoT examples, teaching the inverse-dynamics model to be skeptical of implausible intermediate representations via a consistency regularization loss between CoT content and current observations. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM under our attack suite, measuring trajectory L2 error degradation, collision rate increases, and recovery under adversarial CoT. We compare baseline FSDrive, adversarially-trained variants, and ablations of each attack type, demonstrating improved certified robustness with minimal clean-performance degradation.

title: AdaptiveCoT: Dynamic Switching Between Textual and Visual Chain-of-Thought for Autonomous Driving Under Distribution Shift
description: Problem: FSDrive commits to visual spatio-temporal CoT uniformly across all driving scenarios. However, visual CoT generation is costly and may be unnecessary in simple, familiar situations, while textual CoT may be insufficient in rare, safety-critical scenarios involving unusual geometries or occlusions. An adaptive mechanism that dynamically selects the appropriate CoT modality—or a hybrid combination—based on scene complexity and uncertainty could improve both efficiency and safety. Proposed Method: We introduce a lightweight 'CoT Router' module trained to predict per-scenario CoT modality utility. Given current observations, the router estimates scene complexity via an uncertainty signal (e.g., ensemble disagreement in trajectory predictions or occupancy entropy). Based on a learned threshold, it routes to: (1) text-only CoT for routine scenarios, (2) visual CoT for complex/uncertain situations, or (3) a hybrid cross-attention fusion of both representations. The router is trained end-to-end using a differentiable gating mechanism with a sparsity regularizer encouraging text-only routing when visual CoT adds marginal benefit. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and a synthetically augmented long-tail distribution (fog, occlusion, rare maneuvers), measuring trajectory L2, collision rate, computational cost per inference step, and routing decisions under varying scene complexity. Ablations compare fixed-modality vs. adaptive routing and analyze which scenario types trigger visual CoT.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Corrupted Perception for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning under normal conditions, but autonomous vehicles must also handle degraded perception from sensor noise, adverse weather (rain, fog, night), and sensor failures. Whether visual CoT generation remains reliable and helpful—or actively misleads planning—under such corruptions is unknown. Method: We propose AdverseCoT, which extends the visual spatio-temporal CoT framework by training a corruption-aware future frame generation module. Specifically, we introduce a dual-branch architecture where one branch generates CoT frames from clean synthetic inputs and another from corrupted inputs, with a cross-branch consistency loss that forces robust feature alignment. We augment training data with systematic corruptions (motion blur, rain streaks, lidar dropout) using nuScenes-C benchmarks. A confidence-gating mechanism dynamically weights CoT reliability before feeding into the inverse-dynamics planner, suppressing unreliable CoT under heavy corruption. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C and NAVSIM with injected corruptions, measuring trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and CoT quality (FID, IoU of predicted boxes) across severity levels 1-5. Ablations isolate the contribution of consistency loss versus confidence gating. Baselines include FSDrive and text-CoT VLAs under identical corruptions, demonstrating AdverseCoT closes the performance gap between clean and corrupted conditions by at least 30%.

title: AdverSight: Stress-Testing Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT Robustness via Adversarial Future Frame Perturbations
description:
Problem: While FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT (imagined future frames with lane dividers and 3D boxes) improves planning, the robustness of this intermediate representation to adversarial perturbations remains unexplored. If small, imperceptible corruptions to the generated future frame dramatically alter downstream trajectory decisions, the safety guarantees of visual CoT-based planning are undermined—a critical concern for deployment.

Method: We propose AdverSight, a framework that systematically attacks and hardens visual spatio-temporal CoT representations. First, we design a white-box adversarial attack that perturbs the generated future frame tokens to maximize trajectory deviation while remaining within a bounded visual distance (e.g., LPIPS constraint). Second, we introduce a CoT-consistency regularizer during fine-tuning that enforces invariance of trajectory outputs under small visual perturbations of the CoT frame, using adversarial training with PGD. Third, we propose a lightweight uncertainty-aware CoT validator that detects anomalous future frames via learned normalizing flows before they condition planning.

Experiments: We benchmark on nuScenes and NAVSIM, measuring (1) trajectory error under adversarial CoT corruption, (2) collision rate degradation, (3) robustness gains from adversarial training vs. baseline FSDrive, and (4) detection AUC of the CoT validator on OOD/adversarial frames. Ablations compare white-box, black-box, and patch-based attacks.

title: CausalSceneCoT: Counterfactual Visual Chain-of-Thought for Safety-Critical Scenario Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates plausible future frames as visual CoT, but these represent the most likely future given current dynamics. In safety-critical scenarios (e.g., pedestrian suddenly stepping into road, cut-in vehicles), the critical reasoning requires counterfactual thinking—imagining alternative dangerous futures that haven't yet manifested but could. Current visual CoT frameworks lack this counterfactual causal structure, limiting their utility for proactive safety reasoning.

Proposed Method: We introduce CausalSceneCoT, which augments the visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual branches. Given a driving scene, the model generates not only a most-likely future frame but also K counterfactual 'hazard futures' by conditioning generation on perturbations to agent intent (e.g., pedestrian crossing, vehicle braking). A causal influence module scores each counterfactual by risk severity and proximity likelihood using a learned prior. The trajectory planner then optimizes for safety margins across the full counterfactual distribution via worst-case-aware planning, rather than optimizing only for the expected future.

Experiments: (1) nuScenes closed-loop planning with injected adversarial agent behaviors; (2) CARLA Safety Benchmark measuring collision rates in cut-in, jaywalking, and sudden-braking scenarios; (3) ablation comparing single vs. multi-branch visual CoT; (4) human evaluation of generated counterfactual plausibility. We expect significant collision reduction in rare safety-critical events while maintaining nominal driving performance.

title: AdverseVision-CoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Under Sensor Degradation and Adverse Weather
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT demonstrates strong performance under normal conditions, but real-world deployment requires robust reasoning when perception inputs are corrupted by rain, fog, night conditions, or LiDAR noise — scenarios where visual future-frame generation can propagate or amplify corruption artifacts into planning decisions. Proposed Method: We extend the visual CoT paradigm with a corruption-aware generation framework. A lightweight corruption estimation module first classifies degradation type and severity from input frames. Conditioned on this estimate, a dual-branch architecture generates: (1) a 'restored' visual CoT that denoises structural priors (lane dividers, 3D boxes) via weather-conditional diffusion tokens, and (2) an uncertainty-aware future frame with explicit confidence maps highlighting regions of unreliable prediction. The inverse-dynamics planner ingests both the visual CoT and the confidence maps, learning to down-weight uncertain spatial regions during trajectory generation. A corruption-augmented pre-training stage jointly optimizes restoration quality and downstream planning robustness. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark), CARLA with programmatic weather injection, and real-world adverse-weather driving logs. Metrics include trajectory error under corruption, collision rate stratified by weather severity, and visual CoT perceptual quality (FID, structural fidelity) versus degradation level, comparing against FSDrive and text-CoT baselines.

title: AdverseVisCoT: Robust Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought for Autonomous Driving Under Sensor Degradation
description:
Problem: FSDrive's visual CoT relies on high-quality visual inputs to generate future frames and priors. However, real-world driving frequently involves sensor degradation—rain, fog, nighttime, lens occlusion—causing predicted visual CoT frames to be corrupted or hallucinated, propagating errors into trajectory planning. No work has systematically studied VLA robustness when the visual reasoning chain itself is degraded.

Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseVisCoT, extending FSDrive's framework with (1) a corruption-aware visual CoT generator trained with augmented corrupted inputs paired with clean ground-truth future frames, forcing the world model to denoise and complete visual CoT under adverse conditions; (2) a confidence-gated CoT fusion mechanism that dynamically weights visual CoT tokens based on estimated uncertainty, blending corrupted visual CoT with fallback textual structural priors; and (3) a domain-adversarial pre-training stage that aligns feature distributions across weather/lighting domains to improve CoT generation generalization.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes with synthetic corruptions (fog, rain, night, blur) using established corruption benchmarks, plus real adverse-weather splits (Oxford RobotCar, ACDC dataset). Metrics include trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and visual CoT FID under corruption. We compare against FSDrive baseline, corruption-augmented-only variants, and textual-CoT fallback baselines, demonstrating robustness gains without sacrificing clear-weather performance.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Past-Frame Reconstruction for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning by imagining futures, but VLA models still struggle with causal understanding — distinguishing whether a planned action caused a safe outcome versus correlation with environmental conditions. Without counterfactual reasoning, models may learn spurious shortcuts rather than true causal driving policies.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, which augments visual CoT with counterfactual past-frame reconstruction. Given the current observation and a candidate action, the model generates two visual CoT branches: (1) a factual future frame following FSDrive's approach, and (2) a counterfactual reconstructed frame showing what would have occurred under an alternative action (e.g., braking vs. accelerating). A contrastive planning head compares both branches to select trajectories maximally divergent in safety outcomes. We train using a causal masking objective that requires the model to reconstruct counterfactual scenes consistent with intervention do-calculus, supervised by synthetic perturbations from a driving simulator (CARLA). A differentiable causal graph module explicitly models agent-environment interactions to constrain counterfactual plausibility.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks measuring collision rate, causal attribution accuracy (via interventional probing), and out-of-distribution robustness. Ablations compare factual-only vs. counterfactual CoT and varying numbers of counterfactual branches.

title: AdverseVisCoT: Robust Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought for Autonomous Driving Under Sensor Degradation
description: Problem: Visual spatio-temporal CoT frameworks like FSDrive are trained and evaluated primarily on clean sensor data. Real-world deployment encounters severe sensor degradation (fog, rain, night, LiDAR dropout), where the quality of generated future frames—and consequently the trajectory plans conditioned on them—may degrade catastrophically. No existing work examines the robustness of visual CoT reasoning under such corruptions. Method: We propose AdverseVisCoT, which augments the visual CoT generation pipeline with a corruption-aware conditioning mechanism. Specifically, we introduce a lightweight Degradation Estimation Module (DEM) that infers corruption type and severity from input frames, injecting this as a soft prompt into both the world-model and inverse-dynamics stages. During pre-training, we synthesize degraded future frames using physics-based augmentation (fog rendering, rain streaks, sensor noise) paired with clean ground-truth, training the model to generate degradation-robust structural priors. We further add an uncertainty-weighted trajectory planning head that downweights visual CoT features when estimated degradation confidence is high, falling back to text-CoT guidance. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corruption benchmark), CARLA with simulated adverse conditions, and NAVSIM, measuring trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and FID under 10 corruption types across 5 severity levels, comparing against FSDrive and text-CoT baselines.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Safer Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive advances autonomous driving by imagining plausible futures as visual CoT, but the model only conditions planning on a single predicted future. In safety-critical scenarios, understanding what could have gone wrong—counterfactual futures—is equally important for robust decision-making and rare-event generalization.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, a framework that augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a driving scenario, we generate not only the predicted future frame but also K counterfactual futures by systematically perturbing agent behaviors (e.g., a pedestrian suddenly crossing, a vehicle failing to yield). A lightweight contrastive visual reasoning module compares the nominal and counterfactual visual CoTs, extracting a risk-delta representation that highlights spatiotemporal regions of divergence. The planner is conditioned on both the predicted future and this risk-delta, enabling anticipatory avoidance of low-probability but high-severity events. We train the counterfactual generator using hindsight relabeling from near-miss events mined from real logs, paired with physics-based perturbation augmentation.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM for trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and specifically on rare/near-miss subsets. Ablations compare single-future vs. multi-counterfactual conditioning. We also benchmark on the newly released Waymo Open Dataset safety challenge to assess rare-event robustness.

title: AdverseWorldDrive: Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT Under Distribution Shift via Degradation-Aware Future Frame Synthesis
description:
Problem: FSDrive's visual CoT excels under standard conditions but autonomous vehicles must reason reliably in adverse weather (fog, rain, night, snow) where future frame prediction degrades significantly due to distribution shift in both appearance and physical dynamics. Existing VLA frameworks lack mechanisms to generate physically-plausible visual CoT when sensor inputs are corrupted or visibility-impaired.

Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseWorldDrive, extending the visual spatio-temporal CoT paradigm with a degradation-aware future frame synthesizer. The framework adds two components: (1) a lightweight weather-conditioned adapter that modulates the future frame generator using estimated degradation embeddings extracted from current frames, enabling coherent prediction of degraded future scenes with appropriate uncertainty; (2) a dual-branch inverse dynamics model that separately processes clean structural priors (lane dividers, 3D boxes) and degraded appearance, fusing them via cross-attention before trajectory planning. We introduce a curriculum that progressively trains on clean→light degradation→severe degradation scenarios.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-Fog/Rain splits, the CARLA-Weather benchmark, and a newly constructed NAVSIM-Adverse subset with synthetic corruptions. Metrics include trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and novel 'degradation-conditioned FID' scores. Ablations isolate the contribution of degradation embedding conditioning versus architectural changes, demonstrating improved safety margins in low-visibility conditions.

title: AdverseVisCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Robustness Under Sensor Degradation for Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: Visual spatio-temporal CoT frameworks like FSDrive assume clean, high-quality sensor inputs. Real-world autonomous driving frequently encounters severe sensor degradation—rain, fog, lens blur, LiDAR dropouts—that corrupts both the imagined future frames and the resulting trajectory plans. It remains unknown how fragile visual CoT representations are under distribution shift from adverse conditions, and whether degraded imagined scenes propagate catastrophic planning errors. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseVisCoT, which augments the visual CoT generation pipeline with a corruption-aware conditioning mechanism. Specifically, we (1) train a lightweight degradation estimator that predicts corruption type and severity from raw inputs, (2) condition future-frame generation on explicit corruption embeddings so the world model learns to hallucinate plausible clean structure even from degraded observations, and (3) apply consistency regularization between clean and corrupted visual CoT representations during training to enforce degradation-invariant planning features. A progressive curriculum first trains on clean data, then incrementally introduces synthetic corruptions. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark) and NAVSIM with synthetic adverse weather augmentations, measuring L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and FID of generated future frames across 15 corruption types at 3 severity levels, comparing against FSDrive and text-CoT baselines, with ablations on each component.

title: AdverseChain: Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT Robustness Under Sensor Degradation and Distributional Shift
description: Problem: While FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves nominal driving performance, it remains unclear how imagined future frames degrade under adverse conditions (rain, fog, night, sensor noise) and whether corrupted visual CoTs propagate errors catastrophically into trajectory planning. A failure in intermediate visual reasoning could be more dangerous than no CoT at all. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseChain, which augments the FSDrive-style visual CoT pipeline with a dual-stream uncertainty-aware generation mechanism. A corruption-conditioned encoder explicitly models weather/sensor degradation using learnable degradation embeddings. A confidence gating module evaluates the reliability of generated visual CoT frames via an ensemble disagreement score, dynamically blending visual CoT guidance with text-based fallback reasoning when confidence falls below a learned threshold. We further introduce a corruption-aware curriculum: training progresses from clean scenes to progressively degraded ones, ensuring the inverse-dynamics planner learns to discount uncertain CoT signals. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark), RoboDrive, and synthetic fog/rain augmentations of NAVSIM. Metrics include trajectory error under corruption severity levels, collision rates, CoT reliability scores, and ablations of gating thresholds. We compare against text-only CoT baselines and uncorrected visual CoT, demonstrating that graceful CoT degradation is essential for real-world deployment.

title: VisualCoT Uncertainty Quantification: Calibrating Confidence in Spatio-Temporal Imagination for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive and similar visual CoT frameworks generate a single deterministic future scene as an intermediate reasoning step, but real-world driving involves genuine aleatoric uncertainty (e.g., occluded pedestrians, ambiguous intent). Overconfident imagined futures can propagate errors into trajectory planning, causing unsafe decisions precisely when uncertainty is highest. Proposed Method: We extend the visual spatio-temporal CoT paradigm with an uncertainty-aware imagination module. Instead of generating one future frame, the model produces an ensemble of K diverse imagined futures via stochastic latent sampling, then estimates per-pixel and per-object epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty maps using a lightweight Monte Carlo dropout head applied to visual tokens. A confidence-weighted trajectory planner fuses the K imagined scenes, discounting high-uncertainty spatial regions. Additionally, we introduce a calibration loss that aligns predicted uncertainty with empirical prediction errors during training, ensuring well-calibrated confidence scores. Planned Experiments: (1) Evaluate trajectory accuracy and collision rates on nuScenes and NAVSIM under normal and adversarial/occluded scenarios; (2) Measure calibration quality via Expected Calibration Error on future-frame predictions; (3) Ablate ensemble size K and uncertainty weighting strategies; (4) Compare against deterministic FSDrive baseline and standard epistemic uncertainty methods. Success metric: improved safety in high-uncertainty scenarios without degrading normal-condition performance.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving in Degraded Sensor Conditions
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual CoT framework demonstrates strong performance under normal conditions, but autonomous driving frequently encounters degraded sensor inputs—rain, fog, night-time, lens occlusion—where future frame generation quality degrades significantly, potentially producing misleading visual priors that corrupt downstream trajectory planning rather than improving it. Method: We propose AdverseCoT, which extends visual spatio-temporal CoT generation with a dual-branch architecture: (1) a degradation-aware encoder that explicitly estimates sensor corruption type and severity as conditioning signals, and (2) a robustness-conditioned future frame generator that produces uncertainty-annotated visual CoTs, rendering predicted lane dividers and 3D boxes with confidence heatmaps overlaid directly in the imagined scene. A contrastive pre-training stage aligns degraded and clean visual CoT representations, ensuring the inverse-dynamics planner learns degradation-invariant trajectory conditioning. When uncertainty exceeds learned thresholds, the model gracefully falls back to structural-only CoT (lanes/boxes without background rendering). Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-Adverse (rain/fog/night splits), NAVSIM with synthetic corruption benchmarks, and a newly constructed real-world adverse-weather driving dataset. Metrics include trajectory accuracy under corruption severity levels, collision rates, and CoT quality via FID stratified by weather condition. Ablations isolate the contribution of uncertainty visualization versus degradation conditioning.

title: AdverseFutureSight: Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT Robustness Under Sensor Degradation and Distribution Shift
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual CoT assumes clean sensor inputs at inference time, yet autonomous vehicles routinely encounter adverse conditions (fog, rain, sensor noise, partial occlusion) that corrupt the visual tokens used for future-frame generation and trajectory planning. It remains unknown whether imagined future scenes remain physically plausible and planning-useful under such degradation, or whether errors compound catastrophically through the CoT pipeline. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, which augments FSDrive's training with a corruption-aware curriculum. During future-frame pre-training, we systematically inject paired clean/degraded inputs (using established corruption benchmarks: CommonCorruptions-3D, fog/rain simulation via CARLA) and train an auxiliary denoising head that reconstructs clean visual CoT tokens from corrupted observations before the inverse-dynamics planner consumes them. A lightweight uncertainty estimator flags low-confidence visual tokens, triggering fallback to textual CoT for safety-critical decisions. Planned Experiments: (1) Evaluate trajectory accuracy and collision rate on nuScenes-C (corrupted variant) with/without AdverseCoT; (2) Measure FID degradation of generated future frames under 15 corruption types at 5 severity levels; (3) Ablate the denoising head vs. uncertainty fallback vs. combined approach; (4) Test zero-shot transfer to CARLA adverse-weather scenarios, comparing against text-only CoT baselines to quantify the resilience gap.

title: AdverseWeatherCoT: Robust Visual Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Under Sensor Degradation
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT assumes clean, high-quality visual inputs, but real-world autonomous driving frequently encounters sensor degradation from rain, fog, night conditions, and lens occlusion. Generating physically plausible future frames and reliable trajectory plans under corrupted observations remains an unsolved challenge. Proposed Method: We extend the visual CoT framework with a corruption-aware generation pipeline. During pre-training, we augment the unified VLA with paired clean/corrupted frame data and train a degradation-conditioned future frame predictor that explicitly models uncertainty in occluded or low-visibility regions via probabilistic visual tokens. We introduce a 'clarity confidence map' as an auxiliary CoT element—a spatial heatmap indicating per-region prediction reliability—which the inverse-dynamics model uses to weight trajectory planning. A curriculum first trains on mild degradations, progressively increasing severity, with physics-based rendering for rain streaks, fog density gradients, and motion blur. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark) and NAVSIM with synthetic weather augmentation, measuring trajectory error, collision rate, and FID across degradation types and severities. Ablations isolate the confidence map contribution and compare against standard data augmentation baselines, demonstrating improved robustness without sacrificing clear-weather performance.

title: AdversarialForesight: Stress-Testing Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT Robustness via Targeted Future-Frame Perturbations
description:
Problem: While visual spatio-temporal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves autonomous driving planning, it remains unclear how robust these imagined future frames are to adversarial conditions. If the visual CoT generation is brittle—producing plausible-looking but physically incorrect future frames under distribution shift—downstream trajectory planning could fail catastrophically in safety-critical edge cases (occlusions, rare object configurations, sensor degradation).

Proposed Method: We propose AdversarialForesight, a framework that systematically stress-tests visual CoT robustness by (1) generating targeted adversarial perturbations applied to input observations that maximally corrupt the visual CoT (future frame) while preserving perceptual realism, (2) training a CoT-hardened variant using adversarial augmentation during future-frame generation to improve physical consistency under noise, and (3) introducing a CoT confidence score derived from an ensemble disagreement metric over multiple stochastic forward passes of the world model component.

Experiments: Using nuScenes and NAVSIM, we evaluate: trajectory degradation under adversarial CoT corruption vs. textual CoT baselines; whether adversarial training of the future-frame generator improves out-of-distribution robustness on corner-case subsets (night, rain, occlusion); and whether the CoT confidence score correlates with planning failures, enabling uncertainty-aware fallback to conservative trajectories. We compare against FSDrive and text-CoT VLA baselines on safety metrics (collision rate, displacement error) under multiple corruption severities.

title: CounterfactualDrive: Causal Reasoning via Contrastive Visual CoT for Safety-Critical Scenario Understanding
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive generates plausible future visual CoT for trajectory planning, it lacks explicit causal reasoning about why certain actions are unsafe — a critical gap for edge cases and corner scenarios where the model must understand counterfactual consequences (e.g., 'what if I had not braked?'). Current visual CoT frameworks only imagine likely futures, not alternative dangerous outcomes.

Method: We propose CounterfactualDrive, which extends visual spatio-temporal CoT to counterfactual reasoning. The framework generates paired visual CoT sequences: (1) an intention-conditioned future frame following the planned action, and (2) a contrastive counterfactual frame showing the consequence of an alternative unsafe action. A causal contrastive loss trains the VLA to distinguish safe from unsafe imagined futures, while a lightweight counterfactual decoder generates collision/near-miss visualizations by perturbing ego-trajectory priors and re-rendering 3D object interactions. Planning is then conditioned on the margin between safe and unsafe visual CoTs rather than the safe CoT alone.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the recently released nuPlan safety-critical splits. Metrics include trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and novel counterfactual plausibility scores validated via human evaluation. Ablations isolate the contribution of contrastive visual CoT versus standard single-branch future prediction.

title: AdverseVision-CoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Sensor Degradation for Robust Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning under normal conditions, but real-world autonomous driving frequently encounters severe sensor degradation (rain, fog, night, LiDAR noise). Current visual CoT frameworks are trained predominantly on clean data, causing catastrophic reasoning failures when perceptual inputs are corrupted. No work has investigated whether imagined future frames remain physically plausible—and whether trajectories conditioned on them remain safe—under distribution-shifted inputs.

Proposed Method: We propose AdverseVision-CoT, extending the FSDrive paradigm with a corruption-aware visual CoT generation module. We introduce (1) a degradation-conditioned future frame generator that explicitly learns to denoise and complete partial observations before constructing the spatio-temporal CoT, using paired clean/corrupted scene synthesis; (2) an uncertainty-aware CoT mechanism that overlays confidence heatmaps onto predicted lane dividers and 3D boxes, signaling the inverse-dynamics planner which spatial priors are trustworthy; and (3) adversarial CoT training where randomly corrupted CoT frames are injected during planning fine-tuning to improve robustness.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (synthetically corrupted nuScenes) and NAVSIM with weather augmentation across fog, rain, night, and sensor dropout conditions. Metrics include trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and CoT frame FID under corruption. Ablations isolate each component's contribution to robustness versus clean-data performance trade-offs.

title: RetrospectiveDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Driving Reasoning
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to guide planning, VLA models still lack explicit causal reasoning about why certain actions are dangerous — they cannot distinguish correlation from causation in driving scenarios. A model that only imagines futures may learn spurious shortcuts without understanding counterfactual consequences of alternative actions.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetrospectiveDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual branches. Given a current observation, the model generates (1) an on-policy future frame (following the planned trajectory) and (2) K counterfactual future frames corresponding to perturbed actions (e.g., failing to brake, changing lanes aggressively). A lightweight contrastive CoT selector ranks these imagined futures by safety margin using predicted collision indicators and lane-violation scores, conditioning final trajectory planning on the contrast between safe and unsafe visual futures. This counterfactual visual CoT is trained with a hindsight relabeling strategy: offline driving logs provide ground-truth near-miss events as natural counterfactual supervision.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released Waymo Open Dataset for closed-loop simulation. Metrics include collision rate, comfort scores, and a novel causal intervention benchmark where ground-truth dangerous scenarios are withheld and counterfactual recovery is measured. Ablations compare single-future vs. multi-branch CoT and varying K counterfactuals.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Robustness Under Sensor Degradation and Distribution Shift
description:
Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves nominal driving performance, but it remains unclear how reliably these imagined future frames function as planning priors when input observations are corrupted by adverse conditions (rain, fog, sensor noise, nighttime) or when the domain shifts significantly from training data. A fragile visual CoT could propagate hallucinated spatial priors into trajectory planning, potentially causing worse failures than textual CoT baselines.

Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, which augments the visual CoT generation pipeline with an uncertainty-aware corruption robustness module. During training, we systematically inject structured corruptions into input frames and train the world model to generate physically-consistent future frames despite degraded inputs, using a corruption-conditioned latent bottleneck. We add a confidence calibration head that estimates per-region reliability of the predicted visual CoT, allowing the inverse-dynamics planner to selectively weight uncertain regions. We further propose a consistency regularizer that enforces temporal coherence of lane dividers and 3D boxes across corrupted/clean paired inputs.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (a corrupted nuScenes benchmark) and NAVSIM with injected weather perturbations, measuring trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and visual CoT FID under 15 corruption types at varying severities. Ablations isolate the contribution of uncertainty weighting versus corruption-conditioned generation, comparing against FSDrive baseline and textual CoT methods.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Driving Reasoning
description:
Problem: While FSDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate futures, autonomous driving models lack the ability to perform causal counterfactual reasoning — understanding *why* a chosen trajectory was better than alternatives by visualizing what would have happened under different actions. This inability limits interpretability and prevents learning from near-miss scenarios without real collisions.

Proposed Method: RetroSpectDrive introduces a counterfactual visual CoT framework where, given a completed driving segment, the VLA generates imagined future frames conditioned on *alternative* action hypotheses (e.g., 'what if the vehicle had accelerated instead of braking?'). We train a counterfactual world model using hindsight relabeling: real trajectory outcomes supervise the factual branch, while physically-simulated counterfactual branches (generated via differentiable dynamics perturbation) supervise alternative imaginations. The VLA learns to contrast factual vs. counterfactual visual CoTs to reinforce causal action-outcome associations. A contrastive planning head selects trajectories by visually comparing predicted outcomes across candidate actions.

Experiments: (1) nuScenes counterfactual evaluation with synthesized near-miss scenarios; (2) NAVSIM reactive benchmark measuring collision avoidance under adversarial agent perturbations; (3) human interpretability studies comparing textual vs. visual counterfactual explanations; (4) ablation of contrastive visual planning vs. standard forward-only CoT baselines.

title: AdverseVision-CoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Corrupted Sensor Conditions for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT demonstrates strong performance under normal conditions, but autonomous vehicles must operate reliably under adverse sensor inputs (rain, fog, LiDAR dropout, camera occlusion). It remains unclear whether visual CoT representations degrade gracefully or catastrophically when input frames are corrupted, and no framework currently stress-tests or strengthens visual world-model reasoning under such conditions. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseVision-CoT, which augments the FSDrive paradigm with a corruption-aware visual CoT pipeline. During training, we apply structured corruptions (weather simulation, sensor noise, partial occlusion) at varying severity levels and train the model to generate clean visual CoT future frames from corrupted observations via a denoising world-model objective. We introduce a confidence-weighted CoT fusion module that blends corrupted-observation-derived CoT with a learned prior CoT when sensor reliability is low, estimated via a lightweight uncertainty head. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark) and NAVSIM with injected perturbations, measuring trajectory error, collision rate, and CoT visual quality (FID) across corruption severities. Ablations isolate the contribution of denoising pre-training versus uncertainty-weighted fusion. We also measure cross-corruption generalization to unseen corruption types, demonstrating robustness gains without sacrificing clean-condition performance.

title: AdversarialFutureCoT: Stress-Testing Visual Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in VLA Models via Counterfactual Scene Generation
description: Problem: While visual spatio-temporal CoT improves nominal driving performance, it remains unclear how robust these imagined future scenes are under distribution shift, adversarial conditions, or rare edge cases (e.g., sudden pedestrian intrusions, unexpected road debris). A VLA that hallucinates plausible but incorrect future frames could confidently plan dangerous trajectories—a failure mode invisible in standard benchmarks. Proposed Method: We introduce AdversarialFutureCoT, a framework that deliberately generates counterfactual and adversarial visual CoT frames to (1) stress-test VLA robustness and (2) use hard negatives to improve planning safety. We train a contrastive future-frame discriminator that distinguishes physically-plausible futures from adversarially perturbed ones (object teleportation, lane violation scenarios, occlusion insertions). These adversarial CoTs serve as hard negatives during fine-tuning, forcing the inverse-dynamics model to reject unsafe imagined futures. We additionally introduce a CoT consistency loss that penalizes planning decisions that would be contradicted by multiple sampled future rollouts. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM under (1) standard benchmarks, (2) synthetic rare-event injections, and (3) real long-tail splits. Metrics include collision rate, displacement error, and a new 'CoT-Plan Alignment Score' measuring consistency between imagined futures and executed trajectories.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Causal Scene Understanding in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive demonstrates that forward-imagined visual futures improve planning, but VLA models still lack causal understanding of why certain situations are dangerous — they predict what will happen without reasoning about what could have been avoided. This limits robustness in novel hazardous scenarios where forward prediction alone is insufficient.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual backward reasoning. Given a current observation, the model generates two parallel visual CoTs: (1) a forward CoT imagining the most likely future (as in FSDrive), and (2) a counterfactual CoT imagining an alternative past leading to the current scene under a different ego-action. The inverse-dynamics planner then conditions on both representations, using their contrast to identify causally critical scene elements — obstacles, lane violations, near-misses — that should drive conservative trajectory adjustments. We train this with a contrastive future-frame objective that encourages divergence between counterfactual and factual visual tokens in safety-critical regions, using collision annotations as supervision signal.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released Waymo Open Dataset for interactive scenarios. Metrics include collision rate, displacement error, and a novel Causal Attribution Score measuring alignment between attended scene regions and ground-truth hazard annotations via BEV segmentation overlap. Ablations compare forward-only vs. counterfactual-augmented CoT, and single vs. dual-stream visual reasoning.

title: AdverseVision-CoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Distributional Shift for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates compelling visual CoT for autonomous driving under nominal conditions, but its imagined future frames are trained on clean sensor data. Real-world deployment requires robust reasoning under adverse conditions (rain, fog, night, sensor degradation) where world model predictions may collapse or hallucinate, directly corrupting downstream trajectory planning. Method: We propose AdverseVision-CoT, which augments the visual CoT pipeline with a corruption-aware future frame generation module. Specifically, we introduce (1) a condition-disentangled encoder that separates scene structure from weather/lighting appearance, enabling the world model to generate structurally consistent visual CoT despite corrupted inputs; (2) an uncertainty-weighted CoT fusion that blends multiple imagined futures (sampled under different corruption hypotheses) into a single robust planning token; and (3) adversarial pre-training where the VLA jointly learns to generate and reason over synthetically corrupted future frames via domain randomization. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark), Waymo Open with weather metadata, and CARLA simulations with programmatic adverse conditions. Metrics include trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and visual CoT quality (FID under corruption). Ablations isolate each component's contribution to robustness, establishing how visual CoT degrades gracefully compared to purely textual CoT baselines under distribution shift.

title: VisCoT-Bench: Evaluating Causal Fidelity of Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves trajectory planning, there is no systematic benchmark to evaluate whether the generated visual CoT is causally faithful—i.e., whether the imagined future frames actually drive better decisions or merely correlate with good outcomes. Without such evaluation, it is unclear if models learn genuine anticipatory reasoning or exploit spurious visual shortcuts.

Method: We propose VisCoT-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark with three evaluation axes: (1) Causal Intervention Tests—systematically perturbing generated visual CoT frames (erasing predicted bounding boxes, flipping lane dividers) and measuring downstream trajectory degradation to quantify each visual element's causal contribution; (2) Counterfactual Consistency—injecting adversarially plausible but physically incorrect future frames to test whether planners correctly reject implausible CoTs; (3) Temporal Grounding Score—measuring alignment between visual CoT temporal predictions and actual future sensor observations using optical flow consistency metrics.

Experiments: We apply VisCoT-Bench to FSDrive and three baselines (DriveDreamer, UniAD, text-CoT VLA) on nuScenes and NAVSIM. We conduct ablations correlating CoT fidelity scores with collision rates and displacement errors, and train a lightweight CoT-verifier module that filters low-fidelity visual CoTs at inference time, demonstrating improved robustness in out-of-distribution scenarios including adverse weather and rare agent behaviors.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Causal Driving Understanding
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive advances planning through forward visual imagination, autonomous driving systems still struggle with causal understanding—knowing *why* a near-miss occurred or which past actions led to dangerous states. This limits self-improvement and out-of-distribution robustness. Current VLA models lack mechanisms to reason counterfactually ('what if I had braked 0.5s earlier?').

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, a framework extending visual spatio-temporal CoT to backward causal reasoning. Given an observed outcome (collision, near-miss, or safe passage), the model generates counterfactual past frames—visual 'what-if' scenes showing alternative trajectories and agent configurations that would have led to different outcomes. We train a bidirectional world model that operates both forward (prediction) and backward (causal attribution), using a contrastive visual CoT loss that maximizes divergence between factual and counterfactual imagined scenes for semantically distinct actions. A causal intervention module explicitly perturbs ego-vehicle decisions in latent space before decoding counterfactual frames.

Experiments: (1) Causal attribution accuracy on nuScenes-Safety benchmark, measuring whether counterfactual scenes correctly isolate causal factors; (2) Planning improvement from counterfactual-augmented training vs. FSDrive baseline on NAVSIM; (3) Human evaluation of counterfactual plausibility; (4) Out-of-distribution generalization on Waymo Open Dataset corner cases. This retroactive visual reasoning complements forward imagination, creating a complete temporal causal loop for safer driving.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While FSDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to improve planning, autonomous driving systems still struggle with causal understanding—specifically, knowing *why* a trajectory was suboptimal and what alternative actions would have led to safer outcomes. Current VLA models lack mechanisms to reason about counterfactual scenarios ('what if I had braked earlier?'), limiting their ability to learn from near-misses and edge cases.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, a framework that augments visual CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving segment, we train the VLA to (1) reconstruct the actual future frame as in FSDrive, (2) generate counterfactual future frames corresponding to alternative actions sampled via perturbation of the ego trajectory, and (3) compare the causal divergence between actual and counterfactual visual CoTs to extract a contrastive planning signal. A causal ranking loss enforces that safer counterfactual trajectories correspond to visually distinct, collision-free imagined scenes, grounding causal reasoning in visual space rather than text.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM, measuring trajectory safety under distribution shift, closed-loop collision avoidance improvement, and counterfactual consistency via a new visual divergence metric. Ablations compare textual vs. visual counterfactual CoT, and we test generalization on rare/safety-critical scenarios extracted from nuScenes long-tail splits.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Distribution Shift for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves driving in normal conditions, but its world model may hallucinate plausible-looking yet incorrect future frames when encountering rare adverse conditions (fog, rain, night, construction zones) that deviate from training distribution. This brittleness in the visual CoT propagates errors directly into trajectory planning, potentially causing dangerous failures precisely when robustness matters most. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, which augments the visual CoT generation pipeline with a condition-aware uncertainty module. A lightweight domain-shift detector identifies out-of-distribution inputs and modulates the future frame generation process via stochastic dropout and temperature scaling in the visual token prediction. Rather than generating a single deterministic visual CoT, AdverseCoT produces an ensemble of K diverse future frames representing plausible scene evolutions under uncertainty. A risk-aware inverse-dynamics planner then aggregates these visual CoT candidates using CVaR-weighted trajectory selection, prioritizing conservative maneuvers when CoT variance is high. We further introduce targeted data augmentation during curriculum pre-training using synthetic adverse weather injection. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-night, nuScenes-rain, and Robo-Drive benchmarks measuring trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and calibration under distribution shift. Ablations isolate contributions of ensemble size, uncertainty-guided planning, and adversarial pre-training curricula.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Sensor Degradation for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT demonstrates strong performance under standard conditions, but real-world autonomous driving frequently encounters adverse conditions (fog, rain, night, sensor noise) where future frame generation and visual CoT quality may degrade catastrophically, propagating errors into trajectory planning. No work has systematically studied how visual CoT-based planning fails under distribution shift or how to make it robust. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, extending the visual spatio-temporal CoT paradigm with a degradation-aware generation pipeline. First, we train a condition-aware future frame generator that explicitly models weather/sensor degradation as a latent variable, producing visual CoTs annotated with uncertainty maps indicating unreliable spatial regions. Second, we introduce a CoT confidence-gated planning module that dynamically weights visual CoT features versus raw sensor observations based on predicted CoT reliability. Third, we add a cross-modal consistency loss during training that penalizes planning decisions when visual CoT predictions conflict with available lidar/radar signals. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes with synthetic adverse conditions (FoggyNuScenes, NightNuScenes), the real-world adverse subset of NAVSIM, and the Seeing Through Fog benchmark. Metrics include trajectory error, collision rate, and CoT visual fidelity (FID) across degradation levels, demonstrating that uncertainty-guided visual CoT maintains planning safety where standard approaches fail.

title: RetrospectiveSightDrive: Temporal Consistency via Backward-Forward Visual CoT for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT (future frames) to guide planning, but ignores that past trajectory consistency is equally critical for robust decision-making. Autonomous systems frequently fail when predicted futures are plausible but inconsistent with recent motion history, leading to abrupt trajectory changes. Proposed Method: We introduce RetrospectiveSightDrive (RSDrive), which augments visual CoT reasoning with a bidirectional temporal chain: a backward visual CoT reconstructing a coherent recent-past frame (last 2-3 seconds) alongside the forward future CoT. The backward CoT serves as a 'motion anchor' — the VLA must generate future frames that are geometrically consistent with the reconstructed past, enforced via a cross-temporal consistency loss operating in visual token space. A lightweight bidirectional attention module conditions future frame generation on past CoT embeddings before trajectory decoding. This explicitly models motion continuity and prevents hallucinated futures disconnected from actual vehicle dynamics. Training: We extend the progressive curriculum from FSDrive to include past-frame reconstruction as an auxiliary pre-training task, then jointly optimize backward reconstruction, forward prediction, and trajectory planning. Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM focusing on trajectory smoothness, L2 error, collision rates under occlusion scenarios, and out-of-distribution generalization (adverse weather, rare maneuvers). Ablate backward CoT contribution independently.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Distribution Shift for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates strong performance on standard benchmarks, but visual spatio-temporal CoT reasoning has not been evaluated under adverse conditions (fog, rain, night, sensor noise) that fundamentally alter the appearance of future frames. When the world model generates corrupted or degraded future visualizations, the downstream planner may inherit compounded errors, making robustness a critical open question. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, which extends the visual spatio-temporal CoT framework with a dual-branch future frame generator: one branch produces a clean idealized future scene (structural priors), and a second branch generates a condition-aware degraded future that explicitly models the current weather/lighting context using a lightweight adapter trained on paired adverse-normal driving datasets (e.g., nuScenes-night, ACDC). A cross-attention fusion module reconciles both branches before trajectory planning, allowing the inverse-dynamics model to reason about uncertainty between idealized and degraded futures. We further introduce an adversarial consistency loss ensuring structural priors (lane dividers, 3D boxes) remain stable across degradation conditions. Experiments: Evaluate on ACDC, nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark), and Robo-Drive across 12 corruption types measuring trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and CoT frame quality (FID, semantic consistency). Ablations isolate contributions of dual-branch fusion vs. single degraded/clean CoT baselines.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to anticipate future scenes, current VLA models lack explicit causal understanding of why certain driving decisions lead to unsafe outcomes. Without counterfactual reasoning, models cannot distinguish between correlation and causation in trajectory planning, limiting generalization to rare safety-critical scenarios.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving segment, the model generates 'what-if' visual scenes: imagined future frames conditioned on alternative actions (e.g., earlier braking, different lane choices). These counterfactual visual CoT frames are paired with actual outcomes to train a causal credit-assignment module that identifies which visual features causally influenced trajectory quality. During inference, the model generates both a nominal forward visual CoT and a safety-boundary counterfactual CoT, using the contrast to bias trajectory selection away from high-risk regions. Training uses a hindsight relabeling strategy on nuScenes logs where near-miss events are augmented with synthesized alternative-outcome frames.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes closed-loop simulation, CARLA safety-critical benchmarks, and a newly curated counterfactual driving dataset. Metrics include collision rate under adversarial perturbations, causal attribution accuracy, and out-of-distribution generalization compared to FSDrive and vanilla VLA baselines.

title: CausalChainDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT for Safety-Critical Scenario Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves trajectory planning, current visual CoT frameworks generate a single predicted future, leaving models unable to reason about causal relationships or evaluate 'what-if' scenarios critical for safety-critical edge cases (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, vehicle cut-ins). A model that cannot contrast counterfactual futures may still commit to suboptimal plans. Proposed Method: We propose CausalChainDrive, which extends visual CoT to counterfactual reasoning by generating multiple divergent future frames conditioned on distinct ego-action hypotheses (e.g., brake vs. swerve vs. maintain). A lightweight causal intervention module perturbs the ego-action embedding before future-frame synthesis, producing K counterfactual visual CoTs. A causal ranking head scores each imagined future using a learned safety metric (collision probability, comfort), and the highest-ranked trajectory is executed. Training uses a contrastive objective that encourages divergent counterfactuals to visually differ in safety-relevant regions via localized perceptual loss. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released Waymo Open Dataset safety-critical split. Metrics include collision rate, displacement error, and a novel Counterfactual Discrimination Score measuring how well the model separates safe vs. unsafe imagined futures. Ablations study K counterfactuals, causal intervention strategies, and safety ranking designs.

title: VisCoT-Uncertainty: Calibrated Confidence Estimation for Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: Visual spatio-temporal CoT frameworks like FSDrive generate a single deterministic future frame as an implicit reasoning intermediate. However, real-world driving involves irreducible uncertainty—occluded agents, ambiguous intentions, and multimodal futures. Committing to one imagined future may propagate overconfident errors into trajectory planning, especially in safety-critical scenarios like unprotected turns or dense pedestrian areas.

Proposed Method: We extend the visual CoT paradigm with an uncertainty-aware ensemble of future frames, sampled from a learned latent distribution conditioned on the current scene. Rather than a single imagined frame, we generate K diverse visual CoTs capturing plausible future modes (e.g., agent turns left vs. right). Each visual CoT produces a trajectory candidate; a risk-sensitive aggregation module weights trajectories by epistemic uncertainty estimates derived from disagreement across the ensemble. We introduce a conformal prediction wrapper that provides coverage guarantees on trajectory prediction sets at test time.

Experiments: (1) nuScenes and NAVSIM trajectory planning benchmarks measuring L2 error and collision rate under our multi-CoT scheme vs. deterministic baselines; (2) ablation on K ensemble size vs. compute trade-off; (3) uncertainty calibration evaluation using Expected Calibration Error on held-out near-miss scenarios; (4) qualitative analysis showing diverse visual CoTs capturing multimodal agent behaviors at intersections.

title: AdverseWorldThink: Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT for Autonomous Driving Under Distribution Shift via Adversarial Future Imagination
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates strong performance in standard conditions, but autonomous driving must handle rare, safety-critical scenarios (fog, rain, night, sensor degradation) where training data is sparse and visual CoT quality degrades severely. Current visual CoT frameworks lack mechanisms to generate physically-plausible futures under such distribution shifts, limiting robustness precisely when it matters most. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseWorldThink, which augments the visual spatio-temporal CoT pipeline with a conditional adversarial future imagination module. Specifically, we train a lightweight condition-injection adapter that takes weather/lighting condition tokens as input and modulates the future frame generation to synthesize degraded-yet-physically-consistent visual CoT frames. We further introduce a CoT consistency loss that enforces geometric alignment between clear and adverse-condition future frames, ensuring structural priors (lane dividers, 3D boxes) remain coherent across conditions. A condition-aware curriculum progressively increases adverse scenario difficulty during training. Planned Experiments: (1) Benchmark on nuScenes-Adverse (synthesized corruptions) and real adverse splits, measuring trajectory accuracy and collision rates vs. FSDrive baseline; (2) Ablate condition-injection strategies and consistency losses; (3) Evaluate zero-shot transfer to unseen corruption types; (4) Compare FID for adverse future frame generation against diffusion-based baselines to validate lightweight autoregressive viability in adverse settings.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Sensor Degradation for Robust Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves driving under normal conditions, but real-world deployment faces severe sensor degradation (fog, rain, LiDAR dropout, camera blur). Current VLA frameworks including FSDrive are trained primarily on clean data, leaving an open question: does visual CoT reasoning remain reliable—or even degrade further—under adverse conditions where the generated future frames inherit perceptual corruptions?

Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, extending the visual CoT paradigm with a corruption-aware future imagination pipeline. First, we train a degradation-conditioned world model that explicitly receives sensor corruption embeddings (type + severity) as conditioning signals, enabling it to generate physically plausible future frames that account for degraded inputs rather than hallucinating clean scenes. Second, we introduce a dual-branch CoT structure: one branch imagines the degraded future (what the sensor will actually see), and a second denoising branch imagines the idealized clean future, with a consistency loss aligning their structural priors (lanes, boxes). The inverse-dynamics planner conditions on both branches with learned attention-weighted fusion.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes-C and NAVSIM with synthetic corruptions (fog, rain, motion blur, missing LiDAR), measuring trajectory accuracy, collision rate, FID under corruption, and a new metric—CoT Faithfulness under Corruption—measuring structural alignment between predicted and ground-truth future frames across severity levels. Ablations isolate each branch contribution.

title: VisCoT-Uncertainty: Calibrated Confidence Estimation for Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought in Safety-Critical Driving
description: Problem: While visual spatio-temporal CoT frameworks like FSDrive improve trajectory planning by 'thinking visually,' they provide no principled measure of uncertainty in their imagined future frames. In safety-critical scenarios (occlusions, rare events, adverse weather), an overconfident visual CoT can propagate catastrophic errors into trajectory decisions without any warning signal. Proposed Method: We introduce VisCoT-Uncertainty, which augments visual CoT generation with per-token aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty estimates using lightweight conformal prediction heads attached to the autoregressive visual token decoder. Rather than generating a single deterministic future frame, we produce an ensemble of K diverse visual CoT futures via stochastic sampling with temperature annealing, then compress them into a mean visual CoT with pixel-wise uncertainty maps. The downstream inverse-dynamics planner explicitly conditions on both the visual CoT and its uncertainty map, learning to defer to conservative trajectories when uncertainty is high. We also introduce an uncertainty-aware curriculum that progressively exposes training to harder, more ambiguous scenarios. Experiments: Evaluated on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released nuPlan benchmark, measuring trajectory accuracy under distribution shift, calibration error (ECE), collision rate in high-uncertainty scenes, and human-study evaluation of uncertainty visualization interpretability. We compare against MC-Dropout, Deep Ensembles, and deterministic FSDrive baselines.

title: InteractiveCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought with Multi-Agent Interaction Modeling for Dense Urban Driving
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive generates visual CoT by predicting a single ego-centric future frame, but this representation treats other agents as passive obstacles rather than modeling their interactive behaviors. In dense urban scenarios (intersections, merging lanes), the future is governed by multi-agent negotiations that a single predicted frame cannot adequately capture. Proposed Method: We extend visual spatio-temporal CoT to an interaction-aware paradigm. Instead of one future frame, we generate K conditional future frames, each corresponding to a distinct interaction hypothesis (e.g., yielding vs. proceeding at an intersection). A lightweight Graph Attention Network encodes predicted agent-agent interaction edges from the current scene, conditioning the world model to produce K divergent visual CoT frames. An uncertainty-weighted trajectory planner then aggregates over these hypotheses, selecting trajectories that remain robust across plausible futures. We incorporate a contrastive pre-training objective that enforces semantic consistency between interaction hypotheses and their physical plausibility. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes with a focus on intersection and lane-change scenarios, introduce a new interaction-density split for NAVSIM, and benchmark on the Waymo Open Interaction Dataset. Metrics include collision rate under adversarial agent behavior, trajectory diversity scores, and planning robustness under distributional shift in agent intent.

title: VisCoT-Bench: Evaluating Visual Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Causal Consistency in Autonomous Driving World Models
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning, there is no systematic evaluation framework to assess whether generated visual CoT frames are causally faithful—i.e., whether the imagined future actually drives planning decisions or merely serves as a decorative byproduct. Models could achieve good trajectory metrics while ignoring their own visual CoT entirely, undermining interpretability and safety guarantees.

Proposed Method: We introduce VisCoT-Bench, an evaluation suite measuring three faithfulness dimensions: (1) Causal Intervention Consistency—systematically perturbing generated future frames (removing predicted obstacles, shifting lane dividers) and measuring resultant trajectory changes; (2) Counterfactual Alignment—using a differentiable attention routing mechanism to quantify which spatial regions of the visual CoT most influence final waypoints; (3) Physical Plausibility Score—leveraging nuScenes map annotations and 3D detection ground truth to score geometric coherence of predicted priors against actual scene evolution.

We additionally propose a Faithfulness-Regularized Training objective that penalizes low causal sensitivity between visual CoT and planned trajectories using a mutual information lower bound.

Experiments: Evaluate FSDrive, UniAD, and SparseDrive on nuScenes/NAVSIM using VisCoT-Bench. Show faithfulness-regularized fine-tuning improves both CoT causal sensitivity and collision avoidance in safety-critical edge cases, demonstrating that faithful visual reasoning correlates with safer planning.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to anticipate futures, but VLA models still lack causal understanding of why certain trajectories succeed or fail. Without counterfactual reasoning ('what if I had turned earlier?'), planners cannot learn robust causal policies and remain vulnerable to distribution shift. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, extending visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving scenario, the model generates retrospective visual CoT frames depicting alternative pasts — synthesizing counterfactual future frames conditioned on perturbed actions (e.g., different steering, braking earlier). A causal contrastive loss trains the VLA to distinguish actual trajectory outcomes from counterfactual ones by comparing their visual CoT representations, grounding causal attribution in visual scene differences rather than text. We augment the FSDrive pre-training paradigm with a hindsight curriculum: first reconstructing factual scene evolution, then generating plausible counterfactual branches using diffusion-guided perturbation of object trajectories and ego actions. Planned Experiments: (1) Trajectory planning accuracy on nuScenes and NAVSIM; (2) Counterfactual consistency metrics measuring visual plausibility of alternative scenes; (3) Out-of-distribution robustness on edge-case driving logs from nuScenes-Devkit; (4) Ablations isolating causal contrastive loss vs. standard imitation learning; (5) Human evaluation of counterfactual scene realism.

title: AdverseWorldThink: Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT for Autonomous Driving Under Sensor Degradation and Adverse Weather
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT demonstrates strong performance under standard conditions, but autonomous vehicles frequently operate in adverse scenarios (rain, fog, snow, sensor noise) where future-frame prediction quality degrades significantly, undermining downstream planning reliability. Existing approaches treat adverse conditions as a data augmentation problem rather than a reasoning challenge. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseWorldThink, which extends the visual CoT paradigm to explicitly model uncertainty and degradation in future imagined frames. Our framework adds a degradation-conditioned generation branch that (1) estimates current sensor degradation type and severity from input frames using a lightweight corruption classifier, (2) generates dual visual CoT representations — an idealized clean future frame alongside a degradation-aware future frame that realistically captures what sensors will actually observe — and (3) trains the inverse-dynamics planner to condition on both representations, using the clean frame for geometric reasoning and the degraded frame for sensor-realistic planning. We introduce a contrastive CoT alignment loss to prevent the planner from over-relying on idealized predictions. Pre-training incorporates corrupted nuScenes and synthetic adverse-weather datasets. Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted benchmark), Waymo Open Dataset adverse splits, and CARLA simulated adverse weather scenes, measuring collision rates, trajectory L2 error, and robustness to unseen corruption types compared to FSDrive and standard VLA baselines.

title: VisualCoT Uncertainty Quantification: Calibrated Confidence in Spatio-Temporal Visual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Driving
description:
Problem: While FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves trajectory planning, it lacks mechanisms to quantify uncertainty in the generated visual reasoning chain. A confidently wrong visual CoT (e.g., hallucinated future lane positions or misplaced 3D boxes) propagates directly into catastrophic planning errors, with no way for downstream components to detect or mitigate such failures.

Proposed Method: We augment the visual CoT generation process with aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty estimation.
