Concretely, we introduce a lightweight ensemble of visual token decoders trained with stochastic depth and MC-Dropout during future frame synthesis. Each decoder produces slightly divergent visual CoT frames; their pixel-level and token-level disagreement yields uncertainty heatmaps highlighting unreliable scene regions. These uncertainty maps are injected as additional conditioning signals into the inverse-dynamics planning model, enabling risk-aware trajectory generation that avoids regions with high visual uncertainty. We further propose an uncertainty-gated curriculum: training examples where the visual CoT is highly uncertain are upweighted, forcing the model to improve on difficult, ambiguous scenarios.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM comparing (1) trajectory accuracy under distribution shifts (night, rain, occlusions), (2) calibration curves (ECE) of uncertainty estimates against ground-truth CoT quality, (3) collision rates when uncertainty-gating is ablated, and (4) human evaluation of uncertainty heatmap interpretability.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Understanding
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT improves trajectory planning, autonomous driving systems still struggle with rare safety-critical events (near-misses, cut-ins, sudden braking). Forward prediction alone cannot teach models *why* a scenario was dangerous or what alternative actions would have prevented it. Counterfactual reasoning—'what would have happened if I had acted differently?'—remains unexplored in visual CoT frameworks.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with backward counterfactual reasoning. Starting from a recorded or simulated near-collision outcome frame, the model learns to generate counterfactual past frames by conditioning on alternative ego-actions (e.g., earlier braking, lane change). A dual-branch architecture runs forward prediction (as in FSDrive) alongside a backward counterfactual branch that inverts the temporal chain. The two branches are jointly trained with a contrastive consistency loss ensuring counterfactual trajectories diverge meaningfully from factual ones. A retrieval-augmented dataset mining pipeline automatically extracts safety-critical clips from nuScenes and CARLA logs.

Experiments: (1) Collision avoidance rate on safety-critical nuScenes subsets; (2) Counterfactual plausibility evaluated via FID and human preference studies; (3) Downstream trajectory planning on NAVSIM comparing factual-only vs. counterfactual-augmented CoT; (4) Ablations on backward branch depth and contrastive loss weight.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Causal Understanding in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate future states, but VLA models still lack causal understanding — the ability to reason about why a situation arose and what alternative pasts could have led to safer outcomes. These counterfactual visual CoTs are used as contrastive training signals: the model learns to plan trajectories that diverge from reconstructed unsafe pasts toward safer futures. We enable this through a dual-direction curriculum: forward prediction (as in FSDrive) plus backward counterfactual generation, jointly optimized. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and a newly curated near-miss subset emphasizing rare collision-avoidance scenarios. Metrics include trajectory safety improvement over FSDrive, counterfactual plausibility (FID/FVD of generated past frames), and causal attribution alignment with human driving annotations.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Learning
description:

A dual-branch visual CoT encodes both the 'actual' and 'counterfactual' spatio-temporal sequences as visual tokens. A contrastive planning head learns to prefer trajectories aligned with safe counterfactual CoTs over unsafe actual ones. We introduce a counterfactual consistency loss ensuring generated counterfactual frames respect physical plausibility (lane boundaries, object dynamics). Training augments standard datasets with safety-critical clips from nuScenes-Safety and the CARLA crash corpus.

Experiments: (1) Safety metrics on nuScenes and NAVSIM (collision rate, TTC violations); (2) Counterfactual visual fidelity via FID and lane-adherence scores; (3) Ablation of dual-branch vs. single CoT; (4) Transfer to out-of-distribution scenarios in CARLA closed-loop evaluation; (5) Human evaluation of counterfactual plausibility.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to anticipate future scenes, autonomous driving systems still struggle with causal understanding—knowing *why* a particular action was necessary. Without counterfactual reasoning (e.g., 'what would have happened if I had not braked?'), planners cannot distinguish truly causal features from spurious correlations, limiting safety in distribution-shifted scenarios.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual imagination. Given a driving segment, we train a VLA to generate paired visual CoT branches: (1) the factual future under the taken action, and (2) a counterfactual future under an alternative action (e.g., no braking, lane change). The difference between these imagined frames is used as a contrastive causal signal to reweight trajectory planning, penalizing plans whose counterfactual branches yield higher collision risk. We implement counterfactual branch generation via a conditional diffusion head conditioned on action embeddings, integrated into the FSDrive pre-training paradigm.

Experiments: (1) Closed-loop simulation on nuPlan and CARLA for causal intervention benchmarks; (2) OOD generalization on corner-case splits of nuScenes; (3) Ablation comparing factual-only vs. counterfactual-augmented CoT; (4) Human evaluation of causal explanation quality. We hypothesize counterfactual visual CoT reduces collision rates by 15%+ in rare-event scenarios.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Under Sensor Degradation for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates visual CoT improves planning under normal conditions, but autonomous driving must handle severe sensor degradation (fog, rain, LiDAR noise, camera blur). Current visual CoT frameworks are trained on clean data and generate unreliable future-frame priors when inputs are corrupted, potentially causing overconfident but incorrect planning decisions. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseCoT, which extends the visual spatio-temporal CoT paradigm with a corruption-aware future frame generation pipeline. The framework (1) trains a degradation encoder that conditions future-frame synthesis on estimated corruption type and severity, (2) generates uncertainty-annotated visual CoT frames where structural priors (lane dividers, 3D boxes) carry explicit confidence masks, and (3) conditions trajectory planning on both the visual CoT and these confidence masks via uncertainty-weighted cross-attention, allowing the planner to discount unreliable spatio-temporal cues. We additionally introduce a corruption curriculum that progressively trains from mild to severe degradation during pre-training. Experiments: Evaluate on corrupted nuScenes-C and NAVSIM benchmarks across 8 corruption types, measuring L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and planning robustness gap (clean vs. corrupted performance delta). Ablations isolate the contribution of uncertainty masks, degradation conditioning, and corruption curriculum scheduling.

title: AdverseWeatherCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Under Degraded Sensor Conditions
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual CoT framework assumes relatively clean perceptual inputs, but real-world autonomous driving frequently involves adverse conditions (rain, fog, snow, night) that corrupt visual features and degrade future-frame quality, causing the spatio-temporal CoT to propagate hallucinated or corrupted spatial priors into trajectory planning. Existing approaches handle weather robustness and planning separately, missing the opportunity to reason about degradation within the CoT itself. Proposed Method: We introduce AdverseWeatherCoT, which augments the visual spatio-temporal CoT pipeline with a condition-aware dual-branch architecture. The first branch estimates a degradation map (fog density, rain streak patterns, lighting conditions) as an explicit intermediate visual token sequence. The second branch generates the standard structural priors (lane dividers, 3D boxes) conditioned on the degradation estimate, effectively 'imagining' the scene as if under clean conditions while retaining uncertainty representations. A confidence-weighted inverse-dynamics planner then integrates both the restored future frame and the degradation uncertainty map for trajectory generation. We train using a curriculum that progressively increases weather severity. Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes-weather splits, CARLA adverse-weather benchmarks, and a newly constructed fog/rain augmented NAVSIM split. Metrics include trajectory accuracy under degradation, collision rates, FID of defogged future frames, and ablations on degradation-conditioned vs. unconditional CoT generation.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Safer Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to guide planning, but the model receives no explicit training signal about *why* certain trajectories are dangerous—it never 'sees' the consequences of alternative bad decisions. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual CoT training with counterfactual hindsight imagination. During training, given a recorded safe trajectory, we synthetically perturb it toward near-miss or collision scenarios and task the VLA with generating a 'counterfactual future frame' showing the negative outcome (e.g., rendered bounding box intersections, violated lane boundaries). We then train a contrastive planning head that jointly conditions on both the nominal visual CoT and the counterfactual CoT, learning to maximize trajectory divergence from dangerous futures. A hindsight relabeling curriculum progressively introduces harder counterfactuals as training stabilizes.

Experiments: (1) nuScenes closed-loop simulation measuring collision rate reduction vs. FSDrive baseline; (2) NAVSIM reactive evaluation with injected adversarial agents; (3) ablation of counterfactual difficulty curriculum; (4) data efficiency study showing improved safety metrics with 50% less safety-critical training data; (5) human evaluation of generated counterfactual frames for physical plausibility.

title: VisCoT-Uncertainty: Calibrated Confidence Estimation for Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning by generating future scene representations, it provides no uncertainty estimates for these imagined frames. A confidently wrong visual CoT (e.g., hallucinated obstacles or missed lane changes) can catastrophically mislead downstream trajectory planning without any warning signal. Proposed Method: We introduce VisCoT-Uncertainty, which augments visual CoT generation with per-token aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty maps. Using a lightweight ensemble of low-rank adapter heads on top of the frozen FSDrive backbone, we predict spatially-resolved confidence heatmaps alongside each generated future frame. These uncertainty maps gate the inverse-dynamics planner via an uncertainty-weighted attention mechanism: high-uncertainty regions of the visual CoT receive reduced influence on trajectory decisions, while a fallback rule-based safety module is triggered when global uncertainty exceeds a learned threshold. We additionally propose an uncertainty-aware curriculum that progressively trains on increasingly ambiguous scenarios (occlusions, adverse weather, dense traffic). Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released DriveX benchmark under distribution shift. Metrics include Expected Calibration Error of predicted uncertainty maps, collision rate conditioned on uncertainty thresholds, and trajectory L2 error in high-uncertainty scenarios versus FSDrive baseline, demonstrating that calibrated visual CoT enables safer and more robust autonomous driving decisions.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate plausible futures, but this forward prediction bias causes VLA models to underperform in rare, safety-critical scenarios (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins) where training data is scarce and forward imagination lacks sufficient counterfactual grounding.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual CoT with backward counterfactual reasoning. Given a current observation, the model first generates a 'what-if' counterfactual past frame by inverting plausible near-miss scenarios (e.g., what if the pedestrian were 2 meters closer?), then uses this synthetic retrospective context alongside forward visual CoT to condition trajectory planning. Specifically, we train a counterfactual frame generator using a diffusion-based inverse dynamics model conditioned on hazard annotations, then fine-tune the VLA with both forward future frames and backward counterfactual frames as dual visual CoT streams. A contrastive CoT loss penalizes trajectories that fail to differentiate safe vs. counterfactual-unsafe visual contexts.

Experiments: (1) nuScenes safety-critical subset and CARLA rare-event benchmarks for collision rate; (2) Ablations on forward-only vs. dual CoT; (3) Out-of-distribution generalization on edge-case datasets (e.g., HARD-Drive); (4) Human evaluation of counterfactual plausibility. We expect significant collision reduction in tail scenarios without degrading normal-driving performance.

title: RetrospectiveDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Safer Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate future scenes, but does not leverage counterfactual reasoning—imagining 'what would have happened' under alternative actions—which is critical for learning robust safety-critical behaviors rarely encountered in normal driving. Proposed Method: We introduce RetrospectiveDrive, a framework that augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving segment, we train a VLA to generate counterfactual future frames corresponding to alternative (potentially dangerous) trajectories not taken, using a contrastive visual CoT: one branch imagines the safe executed path, another imagines a collision or near-miss scenario under a perturbed action. The model learns to plan by contrasting these paired imagined futures, explicitly encoding 'why not' reasoning into the visual token space. A hindsight relabeling curriculum mines hard negatives from real collision clips in datasets like nuScenes and Waymo Open, synthesizing counterfactual frames via conditional diffusion conditioned on alternative ego trajectories. Planning is conditioned on both the forward and counterfactual CoT through a cross-attention gating mechanism. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and Waymo Open for trajectory accuracy, collision avoidance in rare-event scenarios, and out-of-distribution robustness. We ablate the contribution of counterfactual branches versus forward-only CoT.

title: VisCoT-Bench: Evaluating Causal Consistency and Physical Plausibility of Visual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal CoT improves driving performance, there is no systematic evaluation framework to measure whether generated visual CoT frames are causally consistent, physically plausible, and actually beneficial to downstream planning—versus being superficially realistic but planning-irrelevant. Models may generate visually coherent futures that violate physical laws or mislead the planner without existing benchmarks detecting this failure mode. Proposed Method: We construct VisCoT-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark with three evaluation axes: (1) Causal Consistency—whether predicted future frames respect causal agent interactions (measured by tracking consistency of predicted boxes across generated frames); (2) Physical Plausibility—automated scoring using physics simulators (CARLA/nuPlan) to check if imagined trajectories of other agents respect kinematic constraints; (3) Planning Utility—counterfactual ablations replacing generated visual CoT with degraded or misaligned futures to measure downstream trajectory accuracy sensitivity. We additionally propose a learned Visual CoT Quality Score (VCQS) trained on human-annotated plausibility ratings. Experiments: We evaluate FSDrive and ablated variants on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and a new adversarial split with rare edge cases (jaywalkers, sudden braking). We analyze correlation between VCQS and collision rate, providing actionable diagnostics for visual CoT-based driving models.

title: VisualCoT Uncertainty: Calibrated Confidence Estimation for Spatio-Temporal Visual Reasoning Chains in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT generates a single deterministic future frame as a planning prior, but real-world driving is inherently stochastic. When the imagined scene is uncertain (e.g., occluded pedestrians, ambiguous agent intent), planning conditioned on a single visual CoT can be overconfident and unsafe. There is no mechanism to quantify or propagate uncertainty from the visual CoT to the final trajectory.

Proposed Method: We introduce UncertainCoT, which extends the visual spatio-temporal CoT paradigm with an ensemble of K diverse future frames generated via latent-space stochastic sampling (using learned noise injection into the VLA's visual token vocabulary). A lightweight uncertainty quantification head estimates per-pixel epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty maps from the ensemble, producing a structured uncertainty-aware visual CoT. The trajectory planner then receives both the mean imagined scene and its uncertainty map, enabling risk-sensitive planning via a CVaR-based trajectory objective that penalizes trajectories traversing high-uncertainty regions.

Experiments: (1) Calibration analysis on nuScenes comparing predicted uncertainty to actual prediction error. (2) Trajectory planning on NAVSIM under diverse occlusion scenarios. (3) Ablation of K ensemble size vs. compute/safety tradeoff. (4) Human study evaluating interpretability of uncertainty-overlaid visual CoTs for driver monitoring systems. Metrics: ECE, collision rate, trajectory L2, and CVaR of scene-level risk scores.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Robust Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate future scenes, but autonomous driving models remain brittle to distribution shifts (adverse weather, rare events) because they never reason about *why* a scenario unfolded as it did. Counterfactual reasoning—imagining alternative pasts—could improve causal understanding and policy robustness, yet no VLA framework exploits backward temporal reasoning as a complementary chain-of-thought. This backward visual CoT is constructed by training an inverse world model on nuScenes sequences to synthesize plausible alternative histories conditioned on hypothetical action perturbations. The dual CoT (future + counterfactual past) is fused via cross-attention before trajectory planning. A contrastive pre-training objective encourages the planner to prefer trajectories whose predicted futures diverge maximally from high-risk counterfactual pasts. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the Corner Case benchmark (e.g., near-miss scenarios), measuring trajectory accuracy, collision reduction, and out-of-distribution robustness, comparing against FSDrive and text-only CoT baselines with ablations on the counterfactual fusion mechanism.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Causal Driving Safety
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive demonstrates that imagined future frames serve as effective visual reasoning scaffolds. Counterfactual reasoning ('what would have happened if I had turned earlier?') is essential for causal understanding but is absent from current visual CoT frameworks.

These counterfactual visual CoTs are used as contrastive planning signals: the policy is trained to prefer trajectories whose imagined futures show lower collision probability compared to counterfactual alternatives. A causal attribution module identifies which spatial regions drove the preference.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes with injected near-miss scenarios, CARLA closed-loop with adversarial agents, and NAVSIM. Metrics include collision reduction, counterfactual realism (FID), causal attribution accuracy against human annotations, and trajectory smoothness. Ablate counterfactual branch contribution and contrastive training signal design.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Driving Reasoning
description:

We use a dual-branch architecture where one branch generates factual future frames (as in FSDrive) and the other generates counterfactual outcomes conditioned on perturbed action hypotheses. title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Autonomous Driving Safety
description: Problem: While FSDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate futures, it cannot reason about near-miss scenarios or safety-critical edge cases that didn't materialize. These counterfactual visual scenes are generated by perturbing predicted 3D object boxes and lane priors under physically-plausible adversarial constraints (e.g., sudden pedestrian emergence, cut-in vehicles). The VLA is then fine-tuned contrastively: safe trajectories are reinforced while counterfactual-triggering trajectories are penalized, using the imagined hazard frames as negative visual CoT anchors. title: RetrospectiveDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Past-Conditioned Scenario Reconstruction for Safer Autonomous Driving
description:

Current VLA models lack explicit counterfactual reasoning—the ability to ask 'what would have happened if I had acted differently?'—leaving them vulnerable to distributional shift in safety-critical situations.

Given a current observation, the model generates two visual CoT branches: (1) the nominal future following the planned trajectory (as in FSDrive), and (2) a counterfactual future depicting an alternative dangerous outcome (e.g., collision trajectory). A contrastive inverse-dynamics planner then conditions trajectory generation on both branches, explicitly optimizing to diverge from the unsafe counterfactual while approaching the nominal future. We train this using hindsight relabeling: real collision events from dashcam datasets (nuScenes, Waymo Open) provide ground-truth counterfactual frames, and safe scenarios are augmented with synthetically rendered collisions via NeRF-based object placement.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and a curated near-miss split of Waymo Open Dataset. Metrics include collision rate, displacement error, counterfactual visual fidelity (FID), and novel safety margin scores measuring trajectory clearance from unsafe regions.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Past-Trajectory Hindsight for Safer Autonomous Driving
description:

A dual-branch VLA processes both the nominal visual CoT and the counterfactual CoT, learning a contrastive objective that maximizes the action-value gap between safe and unsafe imagined futures. We introduce a 'safety salience' attention module that highlights spatial regions where the two CoT branches diverge most, grounding the planner's decisions in causally relevant features. Pre-training follows FSDrive's curriculum but adds a counterfactual generation stage using nuScenes log replay with forced trajectory perturbations.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes closed-loop simulation, NAVSIM, and the newly released Waymo Open Dataset for safety-critical scenarios. Metrics include collision rate under adversarial pedestrian insertion, displacement error in near-miss situations, and counterfactual consistency scores. title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Causal Safety Learning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT improves anticipatory planning by imagining future scenes, but the model cannot distinguish which past decisions causally led to dangerous outcomes versus safe ones. This limits learning from near-miss scenarios and rare safety-critical events where forward prediction alone is insufficient for causal attribution.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, a framework that generates counterfactual visual CoT by reasoning backward from hypothetical future states (e.g., a collision frame) to infer what alternative past actions would have prevented them. The model jointly learns: (1) a forward world model (as in FSDrive) predicting likely futures, (2) a backward inverse-world model that, given a synthesized hazardous future frame, hallucinates what the scene would have looked like had the ego-vehicle taken a safer trajectory. These counterfactual retrospective frames serve as negative visual CoT anchors in a contrastive planning objective, pushing the trajectory decoder away from collision-prone action sequences. Training uses a curriculum alternating between real driving logs and synthetically perturbed near-collision scenarios from nuScenes and CARLA.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes (trajectory L2, collision rate), NAVSIM (PDMS score), and a newly constructed near-miss benchmark extracted from nuScenes edge cases. Ablations isolate the contribution of counterfactual CoT versus forward-only CoT, demonstrating improved causal safety reasoning and generalization to out-of-distribution hazards.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Causal Driving Understanding
description:
Problem: While FSDrive demonstrates that forward-imagined future frames improve trajectory planning, autonomous driving models still struggle to understand causal relationships—specifically, why certain trajectories lead to near-misses or failures. Without counterfactual reasoning, models cannot distinguish between 'what happened' and 'what would have happened if the ego-vehicle acted differently,' limiting safety-critical learning.

Method: We propose RetroSightDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual backward reasoning. Given a real or simulated driving scenario, we train a VLA to generate 'counterfactual visual futures'—imagined frames depicting outcomes under alternative ego-actions (e.g., harder braking, lane change). A contrastive visual CoT pairs the factual future frame with K counterfactual futures, and a causal scoring head learns to rank trajectories by predicted safety margin derived from these visual differences. We introduce a counterfactual curriculum: first training on clear-outcome scenarios (collisions vs. safe passes), then extending to subtle near-miss cases. The counterfactual frames are generated by conditioning the world model on perturbed action tokens.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and CommonRoad-v2 using trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and a new counterfactual consistency metric measuring whether ranked action preferences align with ground-truth safety outcomes. Ablate number of counterfactual branches and training curriculum stages.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning, current VLA models lack causal understanding — they cannot reason about why a trajectory succeeded or failed, nor evaluate alternative actions. This limits their ability to learn from near-misses and edge cases. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual CoT with counterfactual retrospective reasoning. Given a completed driving scenario, the model generates 'what-if' future frames conditioned on alternative actions (e.g., 'what if the vehicle had braked earlier?' or 'what if an adjacent lane change had been taken?'). These counterfactual visual scenes serve as contrastive CoT pairs that train the VLA to associate action choices with divergent spatio-temporal outcomes. We implement this via a dual-branch architecture: one branch generates the factual future frame (as in FSDrive), another generates counterfactual futures conditioned on perturbed action tokens. A causal contrastive loss encourages the model to distinguish safe from unsafe counterfactual outcomes. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM, measuring trajectory safety under adversarial perturbations, out-of-distribution generalization to rare scenarios, and interpretability via counterfactual visual explanations. We also conduct ablations on counterfactual diversity and perturbation magnitude to assess causal sensitivity.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Driving Reasoning
description:
Problem: While FSDrive uses forward visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate futures, autonomous driving models still struggle with causal understanding — distinguishing which perceived scene elements actually caused a planning decision versus which were irrelevant. Without counterfactual reasoning, models may learn spurious correlations between scene features and actions, reducing robustness to distribution shifts.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, which augments the visual CoT paradigm with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving segment, we train the VLA to generate 'what-if' visual CoT frames: imagined scenes where key elements are systematically absent or altered (e.g., removing a pedestrian, changing a traffic light state), then predict what trajectory would have resulted. This counterfactual visual CoT is constructed via a masked future-frame generator conditioned on semantic interventions specified through object-level tokens. A causal consistency loss ensures that interventions on causally-relevant objects produce divergent predicted trajectories, while irrelevant interventions do not. During inference, the model generates both a forward visual CoT (like FSDrive) and a lightweight counterfactual contrast to identify and attend to causally-critical scene elements before planning.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM benchmarks measuring trajectory accuracy, collision rates, and novel counterfactual robustness metrics. We also test out-of-distribution generalization on corner-case subsets and conduct ablations on counterfactual supervision granularity.

title: AdverseWorldThink: Visual Spatio-Temporal CoT Robustness Under Sensor Degradation and Distributional Shift
description: Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that visual spatio-temporal Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves autonomous driving planning under normal conditions, but it remains unclear how imagined future frames used as CoT degrade when input observations are corrupted by adverse weather (rain, fog, night), sensor noise, or domain shift — failures that are safety-critical yet understudied in visual world-model-based planners. Proposed Method: We extend the visual CoT paradigm with a degradation-aware future frame generation module. A lightweight corruption encoder estimates input quality and conditions the world model's future frame synthesis via adaptive layer normalization, producing uncertainty-aware visual CoT frames that explicitly encode confidence regions (e.g., blurred boxes where occlusion is high). We further introduce a contrastive CoT consistency loss that trains the inverse-dynamics planner to remain robust to perturbations in the visual CoT by aligning trajectories generated from clean and degraded imagined scenes. A corruption augmentation curriculum progressively introduces sensor degradation during joint pre-training. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-C (corrupted nuScenes benchmark), synthetic fog/rain augmentations, and cross-dataset transfer (nuScenes→Waymo) measuring trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and CoT frame quality (FID, semantic IoU). Ablations isolate contributions of uncertainty-aware CoT versus standard visual CoT under varying corruption severities.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate futures, but autonomous driving safety critically depends on understanding *why* near-miss events occur — a retrospective reasoning capability absent from current VLA frameworks. Counterfactual thinking ('what if the vehicle had braked 0.5s earlier?') is essential for corner-case robustness yet remains unexplored in visual CoT paradigms.

Proposed Method: RetroSightDrive introduces a backward visual CoT mechanism that generates counterfactual past frames conditioned on hypothetical intervention signals (e.g., alternative steering/braking commands). The model learns a backward inverse-dynamics model that reconstructs 'what the scene would have looked like' under different prior actions, producing counterfactual visual tokens representing avoided collisions or safer lane positions. These backward visual CoTs are then fused with forward visual CoTs from FSDrive in a dual-stream architecture, enabling contrastive trajectory planning that explicitly penalizes trajectories resembling dangerous counterfactual histories.

Experiments: (1) Safety-critical scenario performance on nuScenes-Safety and NAVSIM-CriticalEvents benchmarks measuring collision avoidance under adversarial agent behaviors; (2) Counterfactual frame quality via perceptual metrics comparing generated vs. rendered ground-truth alternative scenarios; (3) Ablation isolating backward CoT contribution; (4) Human evaluation of causal interpretability of generated counterfactual explanations. We expect significant gains in collision rate reduction on tail distributions.

description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate likely futures, but autonomous driving safety critically depends on reasoning about rare, dangerous scenarios where forward prediction alone is insufficient—the model never learns 'what would have happened if I had acted differently.' Given a completed driving segment, we train a conditional future-frame generator to synthesize alternative visual outcomes under hypothetical actions (e.g., 'what if the ego vehicle had maintained speed instead of braking?'). These counterfactual visual scenes serve as contrastive CoT pairs during training: the model learns to distinguish safe vs. unsafe imagined futures by comparing factual and counterfactual predicted frames. A safety-aware planning head is conditioned on both factual and counterfactual visual CoT, learning action selection via contrastive trajectory optimization.

Experiments: (1) nuScenes closed-loop simulation with injected near-miss scenarios; (2) CARLA adversarial benchmark with sudden pedestrian/vehicle cut-ins; (3) ablations comparing forward-only vs. counterfactual CoT; (4) FID and semantic consistency of counterfactual frames; (5) human evaluation of counterfactual plausibility. We expect significant reduction in collision rates under safety-critical edge cases compared to FSDrive baseline.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Causal Understanding in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive demonstrates that forward-imagined visual futures improve planning, autonomous driving systems still struggle to understand *why* a situation became dangerous — the causal roots of near-misses and failures. Counterfactual reasoning ('what if I had braked earlier?') is critical for robust policy improvement but remains unexplored in visual CoT frameworks.

Method: We propose RetroSightDrive, a framework that augments forward visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual backward reasoning. Given a current scene and a reference 'critical event' (collision, hard brake, near-miss), the model generates counterfactual past frames by inverting a learned backward dynamics model, producing visual 'what-if' CoT sequences. These counterfactual visual traces explicitly highlight causal factors (e.g., occlusion, late lane change) and are used as auxiliary conditioning signals during trajectory planning. We train with a dual-direction temporal prediction objective: forward future generation (as in FSDrive) plus backward counterfactual generation supervised via reconstructed historical frames from logged driving data.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the Waymo Open Dataset. Metrics include trajectory accuracy in safety-critical scenarios, collision reduction rate, and a new Causal Attribution Score measuring alignment between generated counterfactual explanations and human annotator judgments of fault causality.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT generates forward-imagined futures to guide planning, but provides no mechanism to learn from near-miss scenarios or understand why a dangerous situation arose. Safety-critical edge cases (sudden cut-ins, pedestrian jaywalking) are rare in forward prediction training, limiting robustness precisely where it matters most. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, a counterfactual visual CoT framework that augments forward future-frame generation with backward causal reasoning. Given an observed near-collision or high-risk scene, the model generates a 'counterfactual past frame' — what the scene should have looked like N seconds earlier to avoid the dangerous outcome — alongside a forward safe-future frame. These paired (counterfactual-past, safe-future) visual CoT representations form a bidirectional temporal chain that explicitly encodes causal relationships between past actions and future safety margins. We train using a contrastive objective: actual dangerous trajectories are repelled from counterfactual-safe ones in the visual CoT embedding space. A risk-sensitive curriculum progressively introduces harder safety scenarios mined from near-miss annotations. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes safety splits, CARLA closed-loop simulation with adversarial agents, and the DriveX near-miss benchmark, measuring collision reduction, out-of-distribution robustness, and counterfactual plausibility via human evaluation. Ablations isolate the contribution of backward reasoning versus forward-only CoT.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Backward Temporal CoT via Counterfactual Past Reasoning for Robust Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT (future frames) to guide planning, but ignores a complementary signal: reasoning about what *should have happened* in the past given the current state. Counterfactual retrospection—imagining alternative past trajectories and their consequences—could strengthen causal understanding of scene dynamics and improve robustness to distributional shift, rare events, and near-miss scenarios.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, a VLA framework that augments forward visual CoT with a 'backward temporal CoT.' Given the current frame, the model first generates a counterfactual past frame representing an alternative unsafe trajectory (e.g., failure to brake, lane intrusion), producing visual evidence of what danger *would have* looked like. This backward CoT is concatenated with the forward CoT from future prediction to form a bidirectional spatio-temporal reasoning chain. A contrastive training objective encourages the planner to maximize trajectory divergence from counterfactual pasts while converging toward safe futures. We pretrain using augmented nuScenes sequences with synthetically perturbed ego-trajectories labeled as dangerous counterfactuals.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes closed-loop, NAVSIM, and Waymo Open Dataset. Metrics include collision rate, displacement error, out-of-distribution robustness (fog/rain augmentation), and near-miss scenario handling. Ablations isolate the contribution of backward CoT versus forward-only CoT baselines.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Driving Reasoning
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive demonstrates that forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT improves planning, but VLA models still lack causal understanding—they cannot distinguish whether a planned maneuver succeeded because of the reasoning chain or despite it. Without counterfactual grounding, models may exploit spurious visual correlations rather than learning genuine cause-effect dynamics. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving scenario, we train the model to generate 'what-if' future frames corresponding to alternative actions not taken (e.g., lane change instead of braking), then use these counterfactual visual scenes as contrastive supervision signals. Specifically, a counterfactual branch generates physically-plausible alternative-outcome frames using the same VLA world model, while a causal preference objective trains the action decoder to prefer actual trajectories over counterfactual ones by measuring outcome quality (collision, comfort). A causal disentanglement loss separates scene-invariant factors from action-dependent factors in the visual token space. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and NAVSIM measuring trajectory accuracy, collision reduction, and a new Causal Consistency Score (CCS) assessing whether performance degrades gracefully under interventional scene perturbations. Ablations isolate contributions of counterfactual frame generation versus causal loss. We expect significant gains in out-of-distribution generalization and reduced spurious correlation exploitation.

title: RetroSpectDrive: Causal Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Safer Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to anticipate what will happen, but autonomous driving safety critically depends on understanding why certain actions are dangerous — knowledge best extracted by counterfactual reasoning ('what would have happened if I had acted differently?'). Current VLA models lack mechanisms to learn from near-miss scenarios or explore alternative action consequences.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSpectDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with hindsight counterfactual imagination. Given a logged driving scenario, we train the VLA to generate not only the future frame conditioned on the executed action, but also counterfactual future frames conditioned on k alternative actions (e.g., harder braking, lane change). These counterfactual visual CoTs are rendered using the same unified visual token vocabulary as FSDrive, encoding spatiotemporal consequences of unchosen actions. A contrastive planning head learns to prefer trajectories whose imagined futures minimize collision probability across the counterfactual bundle. We further introduce a 'regret-weighted' curriculum that upsamples near-collision logged episodes to prioritize safety-critical counterfactual grounding.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the Waymo Open Dataset using trajectory accuracy, collision rate, and a new counterfactual consistency metric measuring alignment between imagined and ground-truth alternative outcomes. Ablations isolate counterfactual count k, regret weighting, and hindsight versus foresight CoT contributions.

title: VisCoT-Uncertainty: Calibrated Confidence Estimation for Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought in Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios
description:
Problem: FSDrive's visual CoT generates a single deterministic future scene representation, yet real-world driving involves inherent uncertainty (occluded agents, ambiguous intent). Planners conditioned on overconfident visual CoTs risk catastrophic failures when predictions diverge from reality. Current VLA frameworks lack mechanisms to quantify or propagate uncertainty through visual reasoning chains.

Proposed Method: We introduce VisCoT-Uncertainty, extending visual spatio-temporal CoT with explicit uncertainty estimation. We train an ensemble of lightweight prediction heads on top of the frozen FSDrive backbone to generate multiple plausible future frame samples, encoding aleatoric uncertainty via per-pixel variance maps overlaid as additional visual tokens. Epistemic uncertainty is captured through Monte Carlo dropout during inference. These uncertainty-annotated visual CoTs are fused into a risk-aware trajectory planner that weights planning decisions by prediction confidence, applying conservative maneuvers in high-uncertainty regions.

Experiments: (1) Calibration evaluation on nuScenes using Expected Calibration Error of predicted future frames vs. ground truth; (2) Out-of-distribution robustness on adverse weather subsets of nuScenes and NAVSIM; (3) Collision rate comparison between deterministic vs. uncertainty-aware planning under occlusion scenarios; (4) Ablation of uncertainty token granularity and ensemble size on trajectory accuracy vs. inference cost tradeoffs.

title: VisCoT-Uncertainty: Calibrated Confidence Estimation for Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FSDrive's visual spatio-temporal CoT improves trajectory planning, the generated future frames are treated as deterministic priors. In reality, future scene evolution is inherently uncertain (occlusions, pedestrian intent, adverse weather), and overconfident visual CoT can mislead downstream planning with plausible-but-wrong futures. Proposed Method: We introduce VisCoT-Uncertainty, which augments the visual CoT framework with explicit uncertainty quantification over generated future frames. Instead of producing a single future frame, the model generates a compact ensemble of K diverse future frames via latent stochastic perturbations using flow-matching with conditional dropout. A lightweight uncertainty head estimates per-pixel epistemic uncertainty maps from the ensemble spread. The planner then ingests both the uncertainty-weighted visual CoT and the uncertainty map as an additional input channel, enabling risk-aware trajectory optimization that naturally hedges against high-uncertainty regions. We further propose an uncertainty-calibration loss that penalizes overconfident predictions in regions where future frames diverge from ground truth. Experiments: Evaluated on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and Waymo Open Dataset. Metrics include Expected Calibration Error of future frames, trajectory accuracy under distribution shift (rain/night), collision rates in high-occlusion scenarios, and computational overhead vs. K. Ablations compare deterministic vs. stochastic CoT and uncertainty-aware vs. unaware planners.

title: AdverseCoT: Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving under Sensor Degradation and Adverse Weather
description: Problem: While FSDrive demonstrates compelling visual CoT for autonomous driving under normal conditions, real-world deployment demands robust reasoning when inputs are corrupted by adverse weather (fog, rain, snow) or sensor degradation (camera blur, LiDAR sparsity). Existing VLA models and visual CoT approaches have not been evaluated or trained for robustness under such corruptions, leaving a critical safety gap. Method: We propose AdverseCoT, which augments the visual spatio-temporal CoT framework with a corruption-aware future frame generation stage. Specifically, we introduce: (1) a degradation-conditioned world model that explicitly predicts future frames under the same corruption type as the input, maintaining consistent visual CoT quality; (2) a cross-condition alignment loss that encourages the latent representation of degraded and clean CoT frames to align, enabling transfer from clean pretraining; and (3) a corruption type classifier that conditions trajectory planning on estimated sensor state. We pretrain on nuScenes with synthetically corrupted variants (nuScenes-C) and real adverse-weather subsets. Experiments: We evaluate trajectory accuracy, collision rates, and CoT frame quality (FID) across 15 corruption types at multiple severities on nuScenes-C and the Waymo Open Dataset adverse-weather split, comparing against FSDrive and text-CoT baselines, demonstrating that corruption-aware visual CoT significantly improves safety-critical edge-case performance.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: FSDrive's forward-only visual spatio-temporal CoT excels at anticipating likely futures but struggles with rare safety-critical scenarios (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins) where low-probability events dominate collision risk. Models trained on forward prediction inherit dataset frequency biases, underweighting these tail cases. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments forward visual CoT with counterfactual backward reasoning. Given a planned trajectory and imagined future frame, the system generates a 'what-if' backward visual CoT by inverting the temporal chain: it hallucinates plausible hazardous precursor states that could have led to a near-collision outcome, then re-plans trajectories to avoid them. Specifically, we train a backward inverse-dynamics model that generates counterfactual past frames conditioned on synthesized collision futures, using these as adversarial visual prompts during planning. A contrastive training objective encourages the planner to produce trajectories that are safe under both forward-predicted and backward-hallucinated scenarios. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released DriveX safety-critical benchmark, measuring collision rate on rare events, trajectory smoothness, and FID of generated counterfactual frames. Ablations compare forward-only, backward-only, and combined CoT strategies, demonstrating that counterfactual visual reasoning substantially reduces tail-case collisions without degrading nominal performance.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT for Safety-Critical Scenario Learning in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual spatio-temporal CoT to guide trajectory planning, autonomous driving models remain brittle in rare safety-critical scenarios (near-misses, sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins) because such events are underrepresented in training data and forward prediction alone cannot expose the causal structure of dangerous situations. These counterfactual visual frames form a contrastive CoT: the model learns safer actions by comparing imagined hazardous outcomes against safe ones, encoded as visual token sequences. A safety-aware reward derived from counterfactual collision likelihood is used to fine-tune the trajectory planner via direct preference optimization (DPO). Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-Safety (curated near-miss subset), NAVSIM, and Waymo Open Dataset, measuring collision reduction, trajectory accuracy in edge cases, and quality of counterfactual scene generation (FID, semantic consistency). title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios
description:

We train using a contrastive objective that maximizes trajectory divergence between safe and unsafe counterfactual conditions, and augment nuScenes with synthetically generated near-collision scenarios via controlled perturbation of ego trajectories.

Experiments: (1) Collision rate on nuScenes and NAVSIM safety benchmarks; (2) Ablation of counterfactual CoT vs. forward-only CoT; (3) Out-of-distribution generalization on rare safety-critical events from the nuPlan dataset; (4) Human evaluation of counterfactual plausibility. title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Learning
description: Problem: FutureSightDrive improves planning by imagining plausible futures, but rare safety-critical events (near-misses, sudden pedestrian crossings) are underrepresented in forward rollouts. These backward visual CoTs are then used as contrastive training signals alongside forward CoTs, teaching the planner to distinguish safe from unsafe trajectory regions in visual embedding space. A dual-curriculum trains the model jointly on forward prediction (as in FSDrive) and backward counterfactual generation, with safety-critical scenarios mined from nuScenes accidents and synthetic perturbations. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and a constructed safety-critical benchmark measuring collision avoidance improvement, trajectory diversity in high-risk zones, and counterfactual visual coherence via FID and human evaluation.

title: RetrospectiveDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Past-Frame Reconstruction for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving

Problem: FSDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT (future frames) to guide planning, but models trained this way lack causal understanding of why certain situations arose—limiting robustness in rare or adversarial scenarios where anticipatory reasoning alone is insufficient. A model that can reason counterfactually ('what if I had acted differently 2 seconds ago?') could better avoid compounding errors and understand causal scene dynamics.

Method: We propose RetrospectiveDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with a counterfactual retrospective branch. Given current observations, the model simultaneously (1) generates a forward visual CoT (future prediction, as in FSDrive) and (2) reconstructs counterfactual past frames conditioned on hypothetical alternative ego-actions sampled via perturbation. A causal consistency loss enforces that counterfactual pasts and observed presents are physically coherent. The retrospective CoT is concatenated with the forward CoT before trajectory planning, providing the planner with both anticipatory and causal grounding.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the newly released Waymo Open Dataset with adversarial scenario splits. Metrics include trajectory L2 error, collision rate, and a new Causal Counterfactual Score (CCS) measuring whether the model correctly attributes near-miss scenarios to specific past decisions. Ablations isolate contributions of retrospective CoT versus forward CoT alone.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Safer Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While FSDrive uses forward visual spatio-temporal CoT to anticipate future scenes, it lacks the ability to reason about why near-miss or unsafe situations occurred — critical for improving robustness in edge cases. Counterfactual reasoning ('what if I had acted differently?') is a powerful but underexplored mechanism for safety-critical driving. Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, a framework that augments forward visual CoT with counterfactual backward reasoning. Given a completed trajectory segment and its outcomes (e.g., a near-collision), the model learns to generate counterfactual future frames corresponding to alternative actions (e.g., earlier braking, lane change) via a conditional inverse-dynamics model trained on contrastive trajectory pairs. These counterfactual visual scenes serve as retrospective CoT, explicitly encoding 'what should have happened' in pixel space. A dual-path architecture jointly processes forward-predicted and counterfactual-generated frames at planning time, using attention-based fusion to bias trajectory selection toward safer alternatives. Training leverages both normal driving logs and safety-critical scenarios mined from nuScenes and the nuPlan dataset using an automatic risk-labeling pipeline. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and nuPlan safety benchmarks, measuring collision rate reduction, trajectory diversity under risk, and counterfactual frame quality (FID, semantic consistency). We also conduct ablations comparing forward-only vs. dual-path CoT reasoning in long-tail scenarios.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT for Safety-Critical Scenario Learning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to anticipate plausible futures, autonomous driving models remain brittle in rare safety-critical scenarios (near-misses, sudden obstacles, adversarial cut-ins) that are underrepresented in training data. Learning purely from observed trajectories fails to expose the model to counterfactual consequences of alternative decisions.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual reasoning. Given a current scene, the model generates not only the most-likely future frame (as in FSDrive) but also K counterfactual future frames corresponding to alternative ego-actions (e.g., 'what if I accelerated instead of braked?'). These counterfactual visual CoTs are produced by a conditional world model that manipulates ego-action tokens before rendering future frames. A contrastive planning head then selects trajectories by comparing predicted safety outcomes across counterfactual branches, explicitly penalizing collision-prone futures. We introduce a counterfactual consistency loss ensuring physical plausibility of alternative scenarios, trained on augmented nuScenes data with synthesized near-miss events.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes-Safety (a curated split of safety-critical clips), NAVSIM challenge, and Carla adversarial benchmarks. Metrics include collision rate, trajectory smoothness, and counterfactual frame FID. Ablations test number of counterfactual branches K and consistency loss weighting.

title: VisCoT-Sim2Real: Transferring Visual Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Across Weather and Lighting Domains for Robust Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: Visual spatio-temporal CoT frameworks like FSDrive generate future-frame reasoning chains trained predominantly on clear-weather, daytime data. When deployed in adverse conditions (fog, rain, night, snow), the imagined future frames degrade in quality, causing cascading failures in trajectory planning—yet collecting real adverse-condition driving data at scale is prohibitively expensive.

Proposed Method: We propose VisCoT-Sim2Real, which learns domain-invariant visual CoT representations by (1) training a lightweight domain-translation module that stylistically transforms generated future frames into target weather/lighting conditions using diffusion-based augmentation, conditioned on sensor metadata; (2) introducing a CoT consistency loss that enforces structural preservation (lane geometry, bounding box positions) under domain shifts; and (3) a curriculum that progressively introduces harder weather domains during fine-tuning, anchored by physics-based degradation priors (visibility models, illumination transforms).

Planned Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes-Nighttime splits, the ACDC adverse-conditions dataset, and a synthetic fog/rain augmented NAVSIM benchmark. Metrics include L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and FID of generated future frames under domain shift. Ablations isolate contributions of diffusion augmentation versus consistency loss. We compare against standard data augmentation and domain-randomization baselines, demonstrating that CoT-level domain adaptation yields superior robustness than pixel-level approaches alone.

title: RetrospectiveDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Hindsight Imagination for Causal Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FutureSightDrive generates forward-looking visual CoT to anticipate future scenes, but VLA models still lack explicit causal understanding—they cannot reason about why a trajectory was safe or dangerous, nor learn from near-miss counterfactuals without real failure data. This limits generalization to rare safety-critical scenarios.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetrospectiveDrive, which augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual hindsight imagination. Given a completed driving episode, we train the world model to generate 'what-if' future frames corresponding to alternative actions (e.g., 'what if the ego vehicle had steered left instead?'). These counterfactual visual CoTs—showing imagined collisions, lane violations, or near-misses—are paired with the actual safe trajectory as contrastive training pairs. A causal credit assignment module learns to associate trajectory decisions with predicted outcome divergence between factual and counterfactual visual futures. During inference, the model generates both nominal and adversarial counterfactual futures before committing to a plan, selecting actions that minimize worst-case imagined outcomes.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes, NAVSIM, and the Waymo Open Dataset, measuring trajectory safety under distribution shift, long-tail scenario performance, and causal attribution quality via interventional probing benchmarks. Ablations isolate contributions of counterfactual generation versus standard forward CoT.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Causal Safety Learning in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: FSDrive demonstrates that forward-imagined visual futures improve planning, but autonomous driving safety critically depends on understanding *why* near-miss events occur—a causal question that forward prediction alone cannot answer. Current VLA models lack mechanisms to reason counterfactually ('what would have happened if I had taken a different action?'), limiting their ability to learn robust safety-critical behaviors from rare events.

Proposed Method: We introduce RetroSightDrive, a framework that augments visual spatio-temporal CoT with counterfactual backward reasoning. Given a current observation and a proposed trajectory, the model generates not only a forward future frame (as in FSDrive) but also a set of counterfactual future frames corresponding to alternative actions (e.g., harder braking, lane change). A contrastive inverse-dynamics head then compares these counterfactual visual CoTs to rank trajectories by causal safety margin—defined as the visual divergence between the chosen and worst-case counterfactual outcomes. We introduce a counterfactual augmentation pipeline that synthesizes near-miss scenarios from logged nuScenes data by replaying alternative ego-trajectories through a neural renderer.

Experiments: (1) Collision rate and displacement error on nuScenes and NAVSIM benchmarks; (2) Causal intervention study measuring whether counterfactual CoT improves behavior on held-out near-miss scenarios; (3) Ablation comparing forward-only vs. counterfactual CoT under distribution shift; (4) Human evaluation of generated counterfactual scenes for physical plausibility.

title: RetroSightDrive: Counterfactual Visual CoT via Backward Spatio-Temporal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Learning
description: Problem: FSDrive's forward visual CoT improves anticipatory driving, but rare safety-critical events (near-collisions, sudden cut-ins) are underrepresented in training data, limiting the model's ability to learn from dangerous situations. Generating counterfactual 'what-if' visual scenarios could dramatically improve safety reasoning without requiring additional real-world dangerous data. Proposed Method: RetroSightDrive introduces a counterfactual visual spatio-temporal CoT framework. Given a completed driving scenario, the model learns backward temporal reasoning: starting from a near-miss or collision outcome frame, it generates a counterfactual visual CoT depicting the avoided-accident trajectory—showing alternative lane positions, adjusted object boxes, and modified background flows. A dual-branch architecture trains simultaneously on (1) forward prediction as in FSDrive and (2) backward counterfactual generation conditioned on outcome frames. The counterfactual visual CoT then supervises a safety-aware trajectory planner that explicitly contrasts safe vs. unsafe action branches. A contrastive visual token loss penalizes trajectories resembling counterfactual dangerous futures. Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes safety subsets, CARLA rare-event benchmarks, and a newly curated near-collision split of NAVSIM. Metrics include collision rate reduction on long-tail scenarios, counterfactual plausibility (FID on safety-critical frames), and trajectory divergence between safe/unsafe branches. Ablations isolate the backward reasoning contribution versus forward-only baselines.
